Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AUR helper or makepkg spawning npm/node to install atomic-lockfile or js-digest · [LLM] eBPF program load or pinned object created from non-system parent on Arch host · [LLM] Persistence written to user shell init or systemd user units from AUR build/install scriptlet
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] AUR build process egress to temp.sh or github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Non-browser process fan-out reading SSH/npm/Docker/AWS/browser credential stores on Arch host · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
AUR helper or makepkg spawning npm/node to install atomic-lockfile or js-digest AIInstallation High
Hunts the core 'Atomic Arch' execution primitive: a PKGBUILD or .install scriptlet invoking npm/node to pull the malicious atomic-lockfile (1.4.2) or js-digest packages. Pairs the AUR build-tool parent (makepkg/pacman/yay/paru/trizen/pikaur/aura) with the specific package strings from the campaign. Rationale: Pairs the article's named malicious npm packages (atomic-lockfile, js-digest from Phase 2 of the kill-chain reconstruction) with the AUR build-tool process tree. Both pivots are required to be present so this is high-specificity — a developer running 'npm install atomic-lockfile' from a normal shell wouldn't have the AUR helper parent.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1059.004 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal threat-research lab intentionally detonating the package on an isolated Arch VM
  • IR team replicating the attack against a known-good baseline for IOC validation
  • Sandboxed CI job in a malware-analysis pipeline pulling the package for static review
  • Future legitimate npm package coincidentally named 'js-digest' published after malware takedown (low likelihood — current malware lookalike)
  • Forensic playback of a previously-infected host's command history via shell-history replay tooling
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("malware-analyst","detlab") and DeviceName !startswith "sandbox-" and DeviceName !startswith "detlab-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the exact ProcessCommandLine and InitiatingProcessParentFileName; identify which AUR package triggered the install by reading /var/log/pacman.log around that timestamp; check pacman -Qi for the source package and its maintainer. 2) Contain: isolate the host from the network, kill any node/npm/Rust-compiled child processes, suspend the user's GitHub/npm/cloud tokens, force-rotate SSH keys, and revoke any SaaS sessions from the affected user. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceId to enumerate every credential file accessed in the next 30 min (UC3), every outbound to temp.sh/fardewoak (UC2), and any new systemd/cron units (UC5). Treat the host as fully compromised — rebuild from clean media per the article guidance.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("npm","node")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile","js-digest")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","bash","sh","fakeroot")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          Parent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          Grandparent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          Child = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm","node")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile","js-digest")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","bash","sh","fakeroot")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AUR Helper Installs Malicious atomic-lockfile or js-digest npm Package (Atomic Arch)
id: 5b8e9d0a-1c2d-4e3f-9a8b-7c6d5e4f3a2b
description: Detects AUR build tools (makepkg, pacman, yay, paru, trizen, pikaur, aura) spawning npm/node to install the malicious atomic-lockfile or js-digest packages tied to the June 2026 Atomic Arch supply-chain campaign.
references:
  - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/400-aur-packages-hijacked-atomic-arch-campaign
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/14
tags:
  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/npm'
      - '/node'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'atomic-lockfile'
      - 'js-digest'
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/makepkg'
      - '/pacman'
      - '/yay'
      - '/paru'
      - '/trizen'
      - '/pikaur'
      - '/aura'
      - '/fakeroot'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*atomic-lockfile* OR *js-digest*) @process.name:(npm OR node) @process.parent.name:(makepkg OR pacman OR yay OR paru OR trizen OR pikaur OR aura OR fakeroot OR bash OR sh)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(npm|node)$/i
| ParentBaseFileName=/^(makepkg|pacman|yay|paru|trizen|pikaur|aura|fakeroot|bash|sh)$/i
| CommandLine=/(atomic-lockfile|js-digest)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.process_path) as image from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm","node") AND (Processes.process="*atomic-lockfile*" OR Processes.process="*js-digest*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.process_path) as image from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("npm","node") AND (Processes.process="*atomic-lockfile*" OR Processes.process="*js-digest*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
AUR build process egress to temp.sh or github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo AICommand & Control High
Hunts the campaign's C2/staging endpoints (temp.sh paste/file-share and the attacker-controlled github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo repo) when the connecting process is an AUR build tool, npm/node, or a shell child of one. Combines process-cmdline mentions (for HTTPS path strings) with network-event hostname matches. Rationale: Pivots on the two article-specific C2/staging endpoints (temp.sh, github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo from Phase 8 of the kill-chain reconstruction) tied to a build-context parent process. The dual pivot (process-cmdline OR DNS/URL) catches both direct git clones of the attacker repo (where the URL lives in argv) and downstream HTTPS uploads (where only DNS/SNI sees temp.sh).
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105 T1567.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DFIR team manually cloning github.com/fardewoak/nodejs-argo for malware analysis (filter on responder hostnames)
  • Developer using temp.sh as a legitimate scratch file-share service from a normal shell (parent will not be makepkg/yay/paru)
  • Reverse-engineering CI job pulling the malicious repo into a sandbox for static analysis
  • Threat-intel ingestion pipeline that mirrors known-bad domains to update IOC feeds
  • Cached resolution of temp.sh from a non-build process that survives in DNS cache and gets attributed to the wrong parent
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("malware-analyst","ir-responder","detlab") and DeviceName !has "sandbox" and DeviceName !has "detlab"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent-process chain (look up InitiatingProcessParentFileName / ParentBaseFileName); pull pacman.log to map the connection back to the AUR package that triggered it. 2) Contain: block temp.sh and the fardewoak repo at the egress proxy; isolate the host; rotate every credential touched on that host (SSH/GitHub/npm/cloud) per the article's IR guidance — these are the assets the stealer harvests. 3) Hunt: correlate this DeviceId with UC1 (atomic-lockfile install) and UC3 (credential file fan-out) to confirm the full kill-chain; expand the search 6h either side of the connection across all Arch hosts to spot other infected machines.
let buildParents = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","npm","node","bash","sh","fakeroot"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (buildParents) or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (buildParents)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak","nodejs-argo")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="ProcessCmdline",
            Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            ChildBin = FileName,
            Detail = ProcessCommandLine
),
( DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (buildParents)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak","nodejs-argo")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="NetworkEvent",
            Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            ChildBin = "",
            Detail = strcat(RemoteUrl, " (", tostring(RemoteIP), ":", tostring(RemotePort), ")")
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let buildParents = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","npm","node","bash","sh","fakeroot"]);
union
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where ParentProcessName has_any (buildParents)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak","nodejs-argo")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Source="ProcessCmdline",
            Detail = ActingProcessCommandLine
),
( ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DnsQuery has_any ("temp.sh")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername=SrcUsername, Source="DnsActivity",
            Detail = DnsQuery
),
( ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where Url has_any ("temp.sh","fardewoak/nodejs-argo")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername=SrcUsername, Source="WebSession",
            Detail = strcat(Url, " UA=", HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent)
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Non-browser process fan-out reading SSH/npm/Docker/AWS/browser credential stores on Arch host AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Rust-based credential stealer's signature behaviour: a single short-lived process reading four or more high-value credential files (~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.aws/credentials, Chrome/Firefox cookie DBs, Slack/Discord session stores) within a short window, while excluding the legitimate browsers/CLIs that normally touch those paths. Rationale: Targets the credential-targets list directly enumerated in the article body (SSH keys, GitHub/npm/Docker/cloud tokens, browser cookies, Slack/Discord/Teams sessions). The article's stealer is Rust-compiled with an opaque process name, so the high-signal pivot is the FAN-OUT (>=4 distinct credential stores in 2 min) by a single unknown binary — that's the smoking gun a normal browser/CLI never produces.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1552.001 T1552.004 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Backup tools (restic, borg, duplicity) snapshotting the user's home directory — touch many credential files in quick succession
  • Dotfiles sync utilities (chezmoi, yadm) on first-run reading every config
  • Configuration management agents (ansible-pull, chef-client, puppet) re-reading host facts/agent creds
  • Endpoint AV/EDR full-disk scans reading every file — exclude by signed AV process name
  • Migration helpers like `gh auth setup-git` or `gcloud auth login` re-reading multiple credential stores in one workflow
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/lib/backup" and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("restic","borg","duplicity","chezmoi","yadm","ansible","puppet-agent","chef-client","falcon-sensor","mdatp")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify InitiatingProcessFileName + SHA256 — if SHA256 is unseen elsewhere in the org and the binary lives under /tmp, /dev/shm, ~/.cache or an AUR build dir, treat as confirmed. Capture the binary for static analysis. 2) Contain: kill the process tree, isolate the host, force-rotate EVERY credential the binary read (the article's IR guidance: SSH keys, GitHub/npm/cloud tokens, browser sessions, Slack/Discord/Teams). Invalidate AAD sessions for the user. 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceId → UC2 (was anything exfiltrated to temp.sh?) and UC4 (was eBPF persistence installed?); pivot SHA256 across the org; review pacman.log for the AUR package that introduced it.
let CredPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.config/glab-cli","Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data","/.config/Slack/storage","/.config/discord","/.config/Teams","/.kube/config","/.vault-token"]);
let KnownGood = dynamic(["ssh","scp","sftp","git","ssh-agent","gpg","gpg-agent","firefox","chrome","google-chrome","chromium","brave-browser","slack","discord","teams","code","gh","glab","aws","docker","npm","kubectl","vault","gnome-keyring-daemon","keepassxc","keyring","snap"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileOpen","FileRead","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (CredPaths) or FileName in~ ("Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data",".vault-token")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownGood)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(FolderPath),
            Targets = make_set(FolderPath, 25),
            First = min(Timestamp), Last = max(Timestamp),
            Reads = count()
          by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, bin(Timestamp, 2m)
| where DistinctTargets >= 4
| order by Last desc
let CredPaths = dynamic(["/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/known_hosts","/.npmrc","/.docker/config.json","/.aws/credentials","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data","/.config/Slack/storage","/.config/discord","/.kube/config","/.vault-token"]);
let KnownGood = dynamic(["ssh","scp","sftp","git","gpg","firefox","chrome","chromium","slack","discord","code","gh","aws","docker","npm","kubectl","vault"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths) or TargetFileName in~ ("Cookies","cookies.sqlite","key4.db","Login Data",".vault-token")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (KnownGood)
| summarize DistinctTargets = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Targets = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            First = min(TimeGenerated), Last = max(TimeGenerated)
          by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, bin(TimeGenerated, 2m)
| where DistinctTargets >= 4
| order by Last desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(PATH OR EXECVE) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_* OR */.npmrc OR */.docker/config.json OR */.aws/credentials OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml OR *cookies.sqlite OR *Cookies OR *key4.db OR *Login\ Data OR */.kube/config OR */.vault-token)) -@process.name:(ssh OR scp OR sftp OR git OR firefox OR chrome OR chromium OR slack OR discord OR code OR gh OR aws OR docker OR npm OR kubectl OR vault OR gpg OR gpg-agent OR gnome-keyring-daemon OR keepassxc)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo TargetFileName=/(\/\.ssh\/(id_|known_hosts)|\/\.npmrc|\/\.docker\/config\.json|\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)|\/\.config\/gh\/hosts\.yml|cookies\.sqlite|Cookies$|key4\.db|Login Data|\/\.config\/(Slack|discord|Teams)|\/\.kube\/config|\/\.vault-token)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(ssh|scp|sftp|git|gpg|firefox|chrome|chromium|slack|discord|teams|code|gh|aws|docker|npm|kubectl|vault|gnome-keyring-daemon|keepassxc)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName], function={ count_distinct=count(TargetFileName, distinct=true) | first_seen=min(_time) | last_seen=max(_time) })
| count_distinct >= 4
ENDPOINT

eBPF program load or pinned object created from non-system parent on Arch host AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the article's rootkit-style persistence primitive: an eBPF program loaded or a BPF object pinned under /sys/fs/bpf/ by a process that isn't one of the legitimate eBPF consumers (Cilium, Tetragon, Falco, systemd-networkd, BCC tools). Particularly noisy when paired with a recent makepkg/pacman/yay parent within the last hour. Rationale: Targets the article's explicit persistence claim — 'eBPF-based persistence to hide processes and file activity' (Phase 5 of the kill-chain). The clean signal is BPF objects pinned by a process that isn't a known eBPF runtime; the leftouter join to recent makepkg/pacman/yay activity raises confidence when the load happens inside an AUR build window.
ATT&CKT1014 T1547 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin running ad-hoc `bcc-tools` like execsnoop, opensnoop, biotop for performance diagnostics
  • Kubernetes CNI upgrade installing a new Cilium/Calico version that hasn't refreshed its process-name list
  • Custom in-house observability agent loading eBPF probes (allowlist by SHA256)
  • Cloud-init or Ansible role provisioning Tetragon/Falco for the first time on a fresh host
  • kernel-debug session via `perf record` writing perf-event maps under /sys/fs/bpf/
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate the BPF object — `bpftool prog show` and `bpftool map show` on the host (read-only); capture InitiatingProcessSHA256 and the BPF object name. If the loading process isn't a known runtime and lives under /tmp / /dev/shm / an AUR build path, treat as confirmed rootkit. 2) Contain: do NOT rely on host-resident tools (they may be hidden by the rootkit) — pull the host out of the network, image the disk from a clean rescue environment, and rebuild from trusted media per the article's IR guidance. 3) Hunt: pivot the loader SHA256 across the org; check every Arch / WSL2-Arch host for `/sys/fs/bpf/` content from non-system processes in the last 30 days; correlate with UC1 (atomic-lockfile install) on the same host.
let KnownEbpfConsumers = dynamic(["systemd","systemd-networkd","systemd-resolved","bpftool","cilium-agent","cilium","tetragon","falco","tracee","sysdig","containerd","runc","crun","docker","dockerd","kubelet","calico-node","snap","mdatp","falcon-sensor","perf","bpftrace"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (KnownEbpfConsumers)
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName in~ ("makepkg","pacman","yay","paru")
    | project AurTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, AurFile=FileName, AurCmd=ProcessCommandLine
  ) on DeviceId
| extend BuildContextNearby = iif(isnotempty(AurTime) and Timestamp between (AurTime .. AurTime + 1h), true, false)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          BpfObject = FolderPath,
          BpfFile = FileName,
          Initiator = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatorCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatorParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          BuildContextNearby, AurFile, AurCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let KnownEbpfConsumers = dynamic(["systemd","systemd-networkd","bpftool","cilium-agent","tetragon","falco","tracee","sysdig","containerd","runc","crun","dockerd","kubelet","calico-node","mdatp","falcon-sensor","perf","bpftrace"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ (KnownEbpfConsumers)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          BpfObject = TargetFilePath,
          Initiator = ActingProcessName,
          InitiatorCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects creation or modification of eBPF objects under /sys/fs/bpf/ by a process that is not one of the standard eBPF runtime consumers (Cilium, Tetragon, Falco, systemd, BCC). Aligned with the Atomic Arch campaign's described 'eBPF-based persistence to hide processes and file activity' when the malware gains root.

Persistence written to user shell init or systemd user units from AUR build/install scriptlet AIInstallation Medium
Hunts post-install persistence dropped by hijacked AUR packages — writes to ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc, ~/.config/systemd/user/, ~/.config/autostart/, /etc/cron.d/, or /etc/profile.d/ when the writer's parent (or grandparent) is makepkg/pacman/yay/paru/trizen/pikaur/aura. Legitimate Arch packages rarely modify the invoking user's home directory. Rationale: Combines two article-grounded signals: the persistence file locations a build-time payload would naturally use (cron/systemd/shell-rc/profile.d/ld.so.preload) AND a writer that is an AUR helper or shell carrying a PKGBUILD/.install context. Legitimate AUR packages install to /usr/... — a write to ~/.bashrc or /etc/cron.d from makepkg's child is the differentiator.
ATT&CKT1546.004 T1053.003 T1547.013
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Shell-framework AUR packages (oh-my-zsh-git, bash-completion variants) that DO legitimately modify ~/.zshrc/~/.bashrc by design
  • AUR packages shipping legitimate systemd units to ~/.config/systemd/user/ (rare but exists — e.g. user-mode VPN clients)
  • pacman hooks updating /etc/ld.so.cache after a library install (different from ld.so.preload but path may confuse)
  • Dotfiles-management AUR packages (chezmoi, stow) intentionally placing files in home
  • First-time provisioning runs where a fresh user account gets its initial rc files populated by an install script
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "oh-my-zsh" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "bash-completion" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "chezmoi" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "stow"
Response runbook
1) Triage: read the actual file content written — `cat` the persistence target and look for the malicious payload signatures (calls to /tmp/.* binaries, references to atomic-lockfile/temp.sh/fardewoak, base64-encoded blobs, ProcID hiding logic). Cross-check the source PKGBUILD against AUR upstream via `pacman -Qi` + `git log` on the AUR repo. 2) Contain: revert the persistence file to its pre-install state (or delete the rogue entry), kill any process started from it, isolate the host. 3) Hunt: pivot on the AUR package name across the org to find every host that installed it; correlate with UC1/UC2/UC3 on the same DeviceId to confirm full kill-chain; remove and quarantine the package from local AUR caches.
let PersistencePaths = dynamic(["/.bashrc","/.bash_profile","/.zshrc","/.profile","/.bash_aliases","/.zprofile","/.config/systemd/user/","/.config/autostart/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/etc/cron.hourly/","/var/spool/cron/","/etc/profile.d/","/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/systemd/system/"]);
let AurTools = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","fakeroot"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (PersistencePaths) or FileName in~ (".bashrc",".zshrc",".profile","ld.so.preload")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (AurTools)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ (AurTools)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKGBUILD",".install","post_install","pre_install","makepkg")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          Writer = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          WriterCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          WriterParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          PersistenceFile = strcat(FolderPath, "/", FileName),
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let PersistencePaths = dynamic(["/.bashrc","/.bash_profile","/.zshrc","/.profile","/.config/systemd/user/","/.config/autostart/","/etc/cron.d/","/etc/cron.daily/","/var/spool/cron/","/etc/profile.d/","/etc/ld.so.preload","/etc/systemd/system/"]);
let AurTools = dynamic(["makepkg","pacman","yay","paru","trizen","pikaur","aura","fakeroot"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (PersistencePaths) or TargetFileName in~ (".bashrc",".zshrc",".profile","ld.so.preload")
| where ActingProcessName has_any (AurTools)
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PKGBUILD",".install","post_install","pre_install","makepkg")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          Writer = ActingProcessName,
          WriterCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
          PersistenceFile = TargetFilePath,
          TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

Tracing Digital Intent: New MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Discovered

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-06-12 9 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Unit 42 has discovered a new macOS Tahoe 26 forensic artifact that tracks user menu selections across the operating system. Learn more here. The post Tracing Digital Intent: New MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Discovered appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1566
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Tracing Digital Intent: New MacOS Tahoe 26 Artifact Discovered
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Anti-forensic deletion/tampering of macOS Tahoe 26 App.MenuItem Biome stream · [LLM] Non-forensic process bulk-reading the App.MenuItem Biome stream
Anti-forensic deletion/tampering of macOS Tahoe 26 App.MenuItem Biome stream AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion or modification of the new macOS Tahoe 26 forensic artifact at ~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local. An attacker aware of this Biome stream would wipe it to erase the menu-selection trail (e.g. the Compress 'stolendata' → Move to Trash → Empty Trash sequence the article describes). Legitimate processes that touch this path are macOS biomed and a small set of system services. Rationale: Hard-anchored to the article's exact path '~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local'. Allow-lists the macOS biome daemons (biomed/biomesyncd) plus /System/Library and /usr/libexec to keep platform housekeeping out. Any other process deleting or rewriting this stream is anti-forensic intent. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cclgroupltd/ccl-segb
ATT&CKT1070.004 T1485
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • macOS minor version upgrade rotating/wiping Biome streams
  • Time Machine restore overwriting ~/Library/Biome contents
  • User-initiated 'Reset all settings' or profile delete on managed Mac
  • Privacy/cleaner apps (CleanMyMac, OnyX) purging cache and Biome data
  • Forensic acquisition tool copying then unlinking the stream after export
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("CleanMyMac","OnyX","DaisyDisk","tmutil","Migration Assistant") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/Applications/CleanMyMac"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on DeviceName and the InitiatingProcess — confirm whether the actor is a known cleaner/IR tool or an unrecognised binary; check user logon context and whether sudo/elevation was used. 2) Contain: isolate the device via Defender, snapshot ~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/ to evidence storage before any further user activity overwrites it, suspend the user's SSO session if the process is unsigned. 3) Hunt: across the fleet, look for the same InitiatingProcess SHA256 in DeviceFileEvents, then sweep DeviceProcessEvents for `ccl_segb_cli.py`, `defaults delete`, `rm -rf ~/Library/Biome`, or `find ~/Library/Biome -delete` over the last 30 days — those indicate attacker recon/cleanup of the Biome system at large.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FolderPath has "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem"
| where ActionType in ("FileDeleted","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","BiomeAgent","runningboardd","launchd")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/System/Library/"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "/usr/libexec/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem"
| where EventType in ("FileDeleted","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","BiomeAgent","runningboardd","launchd")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine !startswith "/System/Library/" and ActingProcessCommandLine !startswith "/usr/libexec/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: macOS Tahoe 26 App.MenuItem Biome Stream Tampering
id: 3a8c4f10-9d23-4c0a-b6e9-7f2a18b9d4c1
description: Detects deletion or modification of the App.MenuItem Biome stream introduced in macOS Tahoe 26 by a process other than known system services.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/new-macos-artifact-discovered/
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/14
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1070.004
  - attack.t1485
logsource:
  product: macos
  category: file_event
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains: '/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem'
  legit_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/biomed'
      - '/biomesyncd'
      - '/BiomeAgent'
      - '/launchd'
  condition: selection and not legit_proc
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR macos) @TargetFilename:*/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/* -@Image:(*/biomed OR */biomesyncd OR */BiomeAgent OR */launchd)
(#event_simpleName=FileDeleted OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten OR #event_simpleName=FileRenameInfo) TargetFileName=/\/Library\/Biome\/streams\/restricted\/App\.MenuItem/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\/(biomed|biomesyncd|BiomeAgent|launchd)$/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/^\/System\/Library\//i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/^\/usr\/libexec\//i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.process_path) as process_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action IN ("deleted","modified","renamed") AND Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_path,"(?i)/usr/libexec/biomed|/System/Library/|/usr/sbin/spindump") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.process_path) as process_path values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action IN ("deleted","modified","renamed") AND Filesystem.file_path="*/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/*" by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where NOT match(process_path,"(?i)/usr/libexec/biomed|/System/Library/|/usr/sbin/spindump") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Non-forensic process bulk-reading the App.MenuItem Biome stream AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a process other than the biome daemons or a known IR/forensic tool opening the ~/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem/local SEGB file. The article confirms this stream contains the verbatim menu items a user selected (Save…, Compress, Move to Trash, Empty Trash) — an attacker reading it can reconstruct admin/user workflow for follow-on social engineering or cover-up. Rationale: Marries the article's exact path with the named open-source parser ccl-segb (and its CLI script ccl_segb_cli.py). Either string appearing in a command line on a production endpoint — that isn't an IR workstation — is high-signal reconnaissance of user intent. We allow-list biomed/Spotlight/Time Machine because those legitimately walk the Biome tree. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cclgroupltd/ccl-segb
ATT&CKT1005 T1217 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DFIR analyst running ccl-segb on a triage workstation as part of an authorised IR engagement
  • Macforensics/Magnet Axiom plug-in performing scheduled artifact collection
  • Internal threat-hunting script piloting the new artifact across the fleet
  • Apple-provided sysdiagnose or feedback assistant capturing Biome state
  • User running a third-party Biome viewer (e.g. mac4n6 tooling) for personal curiosity
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in (dynamic(["IR-MAC-01","IR-MAC-02","FORENSICS-LAB-MAC"])) and InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("ir-analyst","dfir-svc")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the binary (signing authority, hash reputation) and the invoking user — if the host is not a known IR/DFIR endpoint and the user is not in the IR distribution group, escalate. 2) Contain: pull the SHA256 and ccl-segb script body, isolate the device, force AAD/Okta token revocation for the user. 3) Hunt: search DeviceProcessEvents fleet-wide for the same SHA256, for any process with command line referencing other Biome streams (`/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/`), and for outbound transfers from the host of files named like `*MenuItem*`, `*biome*`, or `*.segb` in the next 24h.
let SuspectReads = DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where FolderPath has "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem"
  | where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
  | summarize Touches = count() by DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 10m);
let ProcessReads = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem","ccl_segb_cli.py","ccl-segb","App.MenuItem/local")
  | where FileName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","BiomeAgent")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256;
union SuspectReads, ProcessReads
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","BiomeAgent","mdworker","mds_stores","Spotlight","backupd","tmutil")
| order by Timestamp desc
let FileTouch = ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where TargetFilePath has "/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem"
  | where ActingProcessName !in~ ("biomed","biomesyncd","BiomeAgent","mdworker","mds_stores","backupd","tmutil")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, EventType;
let ProcEvidence = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
  | where DvcOs has_cs "macOS" or DvcOs has "Darwin" or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem","ccl_segb_cli.py","ccl-segb")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/Library/Biome/streams/restricted/App.MenuItem","ccl_segb_cli.py","ccl-segb","App.MenuItem/local")
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, EventType="ProcessCreate", TargetFilePath=tostring(parse_json('{}'));
union FileTouch, ProcEvidence
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",

         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")

| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")

| order by TimeGenerated desc

`o365_management_activity`

Over 400 Arch Linux AUR Packages Hijacked to Deploy Infostealer and eBPF Rootkit

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 17 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Attackers took over more than 400 packages in the Arch User Repository (AUR) this week and rewrote their build scripts to install a credential stealer on any machine that built them. The malware is a Rust binary built to harvest developer secrets. When it lands with root, it can also load an eBPF rootkit to hide itself. The AUR is Arch Linux's community package collection, and it is separate

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Atomic Arch: non-Tor-aware process connecting to local SOCKS proxy on 9050/9150 · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Atomic Arch: outbound HTTP upload to temp.sh from developer/build host · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Atomic Arch: makepkg child spawning npm install atomic-lockfile or bun install js-digest AIDelivery High
Detects the AUR build process (makepkg) spawning npm/bun to pull the malicious atomic-lockfile or js-digest packages whose preinstall hooks drop the deps ELF. Article-specific: these two npm package names are the supply-chain pivot. Rationale: Pivots on the two explicit package names the article names as the Atomic Arch / second-wave installers (atomic-lockfile, js-digest), constrained to makepkg/shell parents so legit npm dev work doesn't fire. Cross-checked with Sonatype's Atomic Arch tracker reference. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Arch maintainer manually testing a benign rebuild that genuinely depends on atomic-lockfile before the package was pulled
  • Internal mirror or research VM running takedown verification scripts
  • Security researcher reproducing the campaign in a sandbox
  • AUR helper (yay/paru) running a forensics dry-run replay
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--dry-run" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "--analyze"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full PKGBUILD and .install script from the affected AUR package (look in /var/cache/pacman/, ~/.cache/yay/, ~/.cache/paru/) and check git history for the suspicious adoption commit. Capture process tree around the makepkg invocation and the host's recent AUR upgrade list. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host from the network; if the binary executed, treat all developer credentials on the host as compromised (browser sessions, GitHub/npm/Vault tokens, SSH keys). Kill any deps process and its systemd unit. Step 3 (hunt): Search the fleet for other hosts that built the same AUR package name in the last 14 days, then enumerate /sys/fs/bpf/ for hidden_pids/hidden_names/hidden_inodes maps to flag rootkit-installed hosts requiring reimage.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("makepkg","bash","sh","zsh","fish")
| where FileName in~ ("npm","bun","node","yarn")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("install atomic-lockfile","install js-digest","atomic-lockfile@1.4.2")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("makepkg","/bin/bash","/bin/sh","/usr/bin/bash","/usr/bin/zsh")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("npm","bun","node","yarn")
| where TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("install atomic-lockfile","install js-digest","atomic-lockfile@1.4.2")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch: deps ELF execution by SHA256/MD5 or src/hooks/deps path AIInstallation Medium
Direct IOC hit on the Rust stealer binary deps. Article publishes SHA256 6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b and MD5 42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40, plus the canonical payload path src/hooks/deps inside the npm package. Rationale: Hash IOCs are published by the article and ioctl.fail; src/hooks/deps is the canonical preinstall-hook ELF location inside the malicious npm tarball. Hits at file-create or process-execute time. Cross-checked vs MITRE T1204.002 and Sonatype Atomic Arch references. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/ • https://www.sonatype.com/blog
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware research VM intentionally detonating the sample
  • Backup/storage system retaining a known-bad cache copy that's read but not executed
  • IR scanner script comparing fleet hashes against this IOC list
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm hash match in the source telemetry; if path-based, cat the file and stat it to confirm size and inode. Identify the parent process that wrote/spawned it (expect makepkg → npm/bun → node preinstall). Step 2 (contain): Isolate host; kill the deps process and any per-user/system systemd unit pointing at /var/lib/<name> or ~/.config/systemd/user/<name>.service. Step 3 (hunt): If the binary ran as root, treat the host as rootkit-capable and pull it for reimage — checking /sys/fs/bpf/ for hidden_pids/hidden_names/hidden_inodes maps. Pivot to all hosts that built the same AUR package in the last 30 days.

( DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 =~ "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
         or MD5 =~ "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
         or FolderPath has "src/hooks" and FileName =~ "deps"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source = "Process", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine ),
( DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where SHA256 =~ "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
         or MD5 =~ "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"
         or FolderPath has "src/hooks" and FileName =~ "deps"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source = "File", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5, ProcessCommandLine="", InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine )
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SHA256 =~ "6144d433f8a0316869877b5f834c801251bbb936e5f1577c5680878c7443c98b"
     or MD5 =~ "42b59fdbe1b72895b2951412222ebf40"

     or ActingProcessName has "src/hooks/deps"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Atomic Arch: systemd unit with Restart=always dropped by non-package-manager process AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the persistence step where deps writes a .service unit under /etc/systemd/system/ (root) or ~/.config/systemd/user/ (unprivileged) with ExecStart pointing into /var/lib/ or user-home directories. Filters legit package managers so only payload-driven drops surface. Rationale: Article explicitly names /etc/systemd/system/ (root) and ~/.config/systemd/user/ (user) plus Restart=always — pairing the path with a non-package-manager initiator strips out routine install activity. Cross-checked vs MITRE T1543.002. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/002/
ATT&CKT1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Ansible/Chef/Puppet config-management runs writing .service units (initiator will be python/ruby/ssh)
  • Custom in-house deployment scripts dropping app systemd units
  • Developer hand-editing a unit under ~/.config/systemd/user/ via vim/nano
  • Container runtimes (podman, docker generate systemd) emitting user units
Suppression filter
| where ActingProcessName !has_any ("ansible","puppet","chef-client","saltstack","podman","docker","cloud-init")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Read the dropped .service unit's ExecStart path and confirm whether it points under /var/lib/<random-name>/ or a user home dir; resolve the SHA256 of the ExecStart binary. Step 2 (contain): systemctl disable --now the unit (and the per-user unit via the affected user's session bus), quarantine the ExecStart binary, and revoke the user's session/SSH keys. Step 3 (hunt): If hash matches the Atomic Arch deps SHA, treat host as credential-compromised and reimage; sweep fleet for matching unit names and Restart=always under unusual paths.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".service"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/","/.config/systemd/user/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("pacman","makepkg","systemctl","systemd-sysv-install","dpkg","apt","apt-get","rpm","dnf","yum","snapd","flatpak")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where TargetFileName endswith ".service"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/","/.config/systemd/user/")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any ("pacman","makepkg","systemctl","systemd-sysv-install","dpkg","apt","apt-get","rpm","dnf","yum","snapd","flatpak"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| regex("(/etc/systemd/system/|/\\.config/systemd/user/)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT regex("(pacman|makepkg|systemctl|dpkg|apt|apt-get|rpm|dnf|yum|snapd|flatpak)$", field=ContextImageFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/etc/systemd/system/*.service" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*.service") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("pacman","makepkg","systemctl","systemd-sysv-install","dpkg","apt","rpm","dnf") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="/etc/systemd/system/*.service" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/systemd/user/*.service") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("pacman","makepkg","systemctl","systemd-sysv-install","dpkg","apt","rpm","dnf") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | sort - lastTime
Atomic Arch: eBPF rootkit pinned maps hidden_pids/hidden_names/hidden_inodes in /sys/fs/bpf/ AIInstallation High
Direct rootkit IOC — the optional eBPF stage pins three named BPF maps under /sys/fs/bpf/ to hide its processes, names, and socket inodes. Article-specific map names; almost zero benign overlap. Rationale: Three map names are taken verbatim from the article and the Whanos reverse-engineering writeup; /sys/fs/bpf/ pinned maps with these names have no plausible benign explanation. High-fidelity rootkit indicator. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1564/
ATT&CKT1014 T1564 T1622
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher loading a benign demo BPF program named identically
  • Detection engineer running this very query's reproducer in a lab
  • BPF observability tooling using overlapping debug names (very unlikely with these specific names)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): On the host, run bpftool map list and bpftool prog show — capture every pinned map under /sys/fs/bpf/ plus its owning PID and program tag. Step 2 (contain): Treat the host as rootkit-active and disconnect from network. The article is explicit: a package manager cannot prove the system is clean. Step 3 (hunt): Schedule the host for reinstall from trusted media, rotate every credential the user touched (browser sessions, GitHub/npm/Vault tokens, SSH keys, Slack/Teams/Discord, Docker/Podman, VPN), and sweep the fleet for the same map names plus for the deps SHA256.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where FileName in~ ("hidden_pids","hidden_names","hidden_inodes")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFilePath startswith "/sys/fs/bpf/"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("hidden_pids","hidden_names","hidden_inodes")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Atomic Arch eBPF Rootkit Pinned Maps
id: 4d6e8a2b-1c3f-4e57-8b9a-2d4e6f8a1b3c
description: Detects creation of pinned eBPF maps named hidden_pids, hidden_names, or hidden_inodes under /sys/fs/bpf/ — the Atomic Arch rootkit fingerprint.

source:linux.auditd @file.path:/sys/fs/bpf/* @file.name:(hidden_pids OR hidden_names OR hidden_inodes)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten

Atomic Arch: outbound HTTP upload to temp.sh from developer/build host AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the stealer's exfil channel — credential bundles posted over plain HTTP to temp.sh. Article-specific exfil destination; not a generic dynDNS pattern. Rationale: temp.sh is the exfil destination named by the article and ioctl.fail IOC bundle. Plain HTTP makes this a clean URL/host-match detection on either web-session or DNS telemetry without needing TLS inspection. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately using temp.sh to share a paste/log file with a colleague
  • Helpdesk staff uploading a diagnostic bundle for vendor support
  • CI job using temp.sh as a transient artifact drop
  • Threat researcher reviewing the campaign's exfil endpoint from a sandbox
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","msedge","thunderbird") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/var/lib/","/tmp/","/home/","/.cache/","/.config/")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Identify the initiating process and folder path — if it's a non-browser, non-curl process running out of /var/lib/, /tmp/, or a user home, treat as confirmed exfil. Pull the host's recent AUR build history. Step 2 (contain): Sinkhole temp.sh at the proxy/firewall (or block-list the resolved IPs), isolate the host, and revoke every developer credential the stealer scope lists (browser, GitHub, npm, Vault, OpenAI, Slack/Teams/Discord, Docker/Podman, SSH). Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the initiating process binary's SHA256 and check fleet-wide; correlate with the systemd-persistence and BPF-map UCs above to identify other compromised hosts.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteUrl has "temp.sh" or RemoteUrl endswith ".temp.sh"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where HttpHostName endswith "temp.sh" or Url has "temp.sh"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, HttpMethod, HttpHostName, Url, HttpRequestBodyBytes, DstIpAddr
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Outbound Upload to temp.sh File-Sharing Service

#event_simpleName=DnsRequest

Atomic Arch: non-Tor-aware process connecting to local SOCKS proxy on 9050/9150 AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the C2 channel — the stealer routes through a localhost Tor SOCKS proxy on 9050/9150. Detection focuses on dev/build hosts where Tor traffic to onion services is not part of the normal workflow. Rationale: Article notes C2 via Tor onion through a local loopback proxy; 9050/9150 are the canonical Tor SOCKS ports. Suppressing the small set of legitimate Tor processes turns this into a high-fidelity dev-host indicator. Sentinel ImNetworkSession lacks process context so we lean on 5-tuple plus a count threshold to bias toward sustained beaconing. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1573/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1573 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running torsocks or proxychains for legitimate access to onion services
  • Privacy-conscious user running their own Tor client for personal traffic
  • Researcher analyzing onion infrastructure from a workstation
  • Tails/Whonix-style hardened workstation pattern leaking to corporate telemetry
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the initiating process SHA256 and command line — match against the deps IOC and check FolderPath for /var/lib/, /tmp/, or user-home origin. Confirm tor binary is actually present and running on host. Step 2 (contain): Kill the offending process and its parent systemd unit; block 9050/9150 outbound at host firewall except for sanctioned Tor processes. Step 3 (hunt): Resolve the host's DNS history for the onion bootstrap domains (consensus directory authorities, *.torproject.org), correlate with the temp.sh exfil UC, and pivot to other dev hosts on the same subnet with loopback Tor connections.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Loopback" or RemoteIP in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where RemotePort in (9050, 9150)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("tor","torbrowser-launcher","firefox","firefox-esr","brave","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("127.0.0.1","::1")
| where DstPortNumber in (9050, 9150)
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Non-Tor Process Connecting to Local SOCKS Proxy 9050 or 9150
id: 7a2c5d9e-3b4f-4108-9d2e-5f6a7b8c9d0e
description: Detects processes other than Tor itself or Tor-aware browsers connecting to the local Tor SOCKS proxy ports — matching Atomic Arch C2 routing.

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Traffic.process_name) as process_name values(All_Traffic.user) as user from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("127.0.0.1","::1") AND All_Traffic.dest_port IN (9050,9150) AND NOT All_Traffic.process_name IN ("tor","firefox","torbrowser-launcher","brave","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_name All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | sort - lastTime
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.

| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*

    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
