Atomic Arch rootkit — eBPF program load by AUR-build-chain descendant AIInstallation Medium
Detects loading of an eBPF program by a process whose ancestor chain includes pacman/makepkg/npm/node or the 'deps' ELF — the privilege-escalation step of the Atomic Arch rootkit. Legitimate eBPF users (systemd, kubelet, cilium, bpftool) are excluded; the campaign uses bpf() syscalls to install a kernel-resident process/file/network hider. Rationale: The article explicitly states the malware uses eBPF for kernel-level execution and hiding ("the malware can run inside the kernel with elevated privileges and hide local processes"). bpf() syscall and BPF_PROG_LOAD are the auditd-visible signals of eBPF loading. Restricting the ancestor chain to pacman/makepkg/npm/node/deps removes legitimate eBPF users. Falcon LogScale left empty — FDR doesn't ship a dedicated bpf-syscall event in the documented schema. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1014/ • https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/bpf/
ATT&CKT1068 T1014 T1547
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer on an Arch host running bcc/bpftrace/perf tools manually for performance work
  • tcpdump or wireshark loading XDP/BPF socket filters under sudo
  • Newly-installed eBPF-using observability agents (Pixie, Parca, Inspektor Gadget) on dev boxes
  • Container runtimes other than the excluded set (podman with seccomp BPF) when started from a shell
  • Cilium or other CNI plugins running outside their normal service path during debugging
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bpftrace","bcc-tools","perf record","tcpdump","bpftool"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the loading process and its full ancestor chain; if rooted at pacman/makepkg, this is almost certainly malicious. Capture `bpftool prog show` and `bpftool map show` output and snapshot /sys/fs/bpf. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host immediately — an eBPF rootkit can hide processes from EDR. Reboot to a known-good kernel/initrd and image the disk before wiping. Step 3 (hunt): Compare userland `ps`/`ss`/`ls /proc` against kernel-visible lists via auditd or `/proc/<pid>/status` directly; alert on discrepancies. Sweep org for any host with eBPF programs persisted across reboots that aren't owned by a known service.
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("BpfProgramLoaded","SyscallAudit","EBPFActivity")
   or AdditionalFields has_any ("BPF_PROG_LOAD","sys_bpf","CAP_BPF","type=BPF")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("systemd","systemd-bpf","kubelet","cilium-agent","bpftool","containerd","dockerd","falcon-sensor","runc")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("pacman","makepkg","npm","node","sh","bash")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName == "deps"
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("atomic-lockfile","/deps")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AdditionalFields
| order by Timestamp desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in~ ("auth","authpriv","user","kern","daemon") or ProcessName has_any ("auditd","kauditd","audisp")
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("BPF_PROG_LOAD","type=BPF","CAP_BPF","sys_bpf","syscall=321")
| where not(SyslogMessage has_any ("systemd","kubelet","cilium","bpftool","containerd","dockerd","falcon-sensor","runc"))
| where SyslogMessage has_any ("pacman","makepkg","npm"," node ","atomic-lockfile","/deps","comm=\"deps\"")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, Facility, ProcessName, SyslogMessage
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:linux.auditd (@auditd.type:BPF OR @auditd.syscall:bpf OR @process.command_line:(*BPF_PROG_LOAD* OR *sys_bpf*)) -@process.executable.path:(*\/systemd* OR *\/kubelet OR *\/cilium* OR *\/bpftool OR *\/containerd OR *\/dockerd OR *\/falcon-sensor)
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*BPF_PROG_LOAD*" OR Processes.process="*bpf(*" OR Processes.process="*sys_bpf*" OR Processes.process="*CAP_BPF*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("pacman","makepkg","npm","node","sh","bash","deps") AND NOT Processes.process_name IN ("systemd","kubelet","cilium-agent","bpftool","containerd","dockerd") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*BPF_PROG_LOAD*" OR Processes.process="*bpf(*" OR Processes.process="*sys_bpf*" OR Processes.process="*CAP_BPF*") AND Processes.parent_process_name IN ("pacman","makepkg","npm","node","sh","bash","deps") AND NOT Processes.process_name IN ("systemd","kubelet","cilium-agent","bpftool","containerd","dockerd") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Atomic Arch infostealer — bulk reads of SSH/npmrc/Vault/browser-cookie files by non-shell process AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the Atomic Arch 'deps' ELF (or any non-legitimate process) reading multiple credential files in sequence: ~/.ssh/id_*, ~/.npmrc, ~/.docker/config.json, ~/.vault-token, browser cookie SQLite DBs, and Slack/Teams/Discord local stores. The fan-out across these specific paths from a single short-lived process is the campaign's credential-harvesting signature. Rationale: Whanos' analysis (cited in the article) enumerates the exact set of credential stores 'deps' targets: GitHub/npm tokens, SSH artifacts, HashiCorp Vault tokens, browser cookies, Slack/Teams/Discord/Telegram data, Docker/Podman config, shell histories. Detecting a non-legit process that reads four or more of these in a short window is far more specific than any single-file watch. Cross-checked Sonatype's binary-string list against the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dotfile-sync tools (yadm, chezmoi, stow) iterating over ~/.ssh + ~/.npmrc + ~/.docker on first run
  • Backup agents (restic, borg, duplicity, BorgBase) reading user home as part of a scheduled snapshot
  • Indexers like Tracker3/Recoll/baloo touching all user files including credential stores
  • DevSecOps secret scanners run manually (trufflehog, gitleaks, semgrep secrets)
  • Migration scripts moving a user profile between hosts
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("yadm","chezmoi","stow","restic","borg","duplicity","tracker-miner-fs-3","baloo_file","trufflehog","gitleaks"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the reading process binary — if it's the 'deps' ELF or any unsigned binary under ~/.npm, ~/.cache, or /tmp, treat as confirmed. Snapshot the process's open file descriptors and network connections via /proc. Step 2 (contain): Kill the process tree, isolate the host, immediately revoke all credentials whose files were touched: rotate SSH keys, regenerate GitHub PATs and npm tokens, revoke and re-issue HashiCorp Vault tokens, force browser cookie invalidation, and reset Slack/Teams/Discord sessions. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the SSH keys' authorized_keys distribution across the fleet; check GitHub audit log for new SSH-key uploads or PAT creations from the user; check Vault audit log for token-use from unusual IPs; sweep for the same process binary on other developer workstations.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRead","FileOpened","FileAccessed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/", "/.npmrc", "/.docker/config.json", "/.vault-token", "/.config/Slack/", "/.config/discord/", "/.config/Microsoft/Teams/", "/.mozilla/firefox/", "/snap/firefox", "/.config/google-chrome/", "/.config/chromium/")
   or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","cookies.sqlite","Cookies","Login Data",".vault-token",".npmrc")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sshd","ssh","scp","sftp","ssh-agent","gpg-agent","git","firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","slack","teams","discord","keepassxc","gnome-keyring-d","systemd","systemd-user","cron","tar","rsync","backup")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), DistinctPaths=dcount(FolderPath), SamplePaths=make_set(FolderPath, 20), SampleFiles=make_set(FileName, 20) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| where DistinctPaths >= 4
| order by FirstSeen desc
Syslog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Facility in~ ("auth","authpriv","user") or ProcessName has_any ("auditd","kauditd")
| extend SensitivePath = case(
    SyslogMessage has "/.ssh/id_", "ssh_key",
    SyslogMessage has "/.npmrc", "npmrc",
    SyslogMessage has "/.docker/config.json", "docker_cfg",
    SyslogMessage has ".vault-token", "vault_token",
    SyslogMessage has "/.config/Slack", "slack",
    SyslogMessage has "/.config/discord", "discord",
    SyslogMessage has "/Microsoft/Teams", "teams",
    SyslogMessage has "cookies.sqlite", "browser_cookies",
    SyslogMessage has "Login Data", "browser_login",
    "")
| where isnotempty(SensitivePath)
| where not(SyslogMessage has_any ("comm=\"ssh\"","comm=\"sshd\"","comm=\"gpg-agent\"","comm=\"firefox\"","comm=\"chrome\"","comm=\"slack\"","comm=\"teams\"","comm=\"discord\"","comm=\"keepassxc\""))
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), DistinctPaths=dcount(SensitivePath), Paths=make_set(SensitivePath) by Computer, HostName, ProcessName
| where DistinctPaths >= 4
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:(SYSCALL OR PATH) @file.path:(*\/.ssh\/id_* OR *\/.npmrc OR *\/.docker\/config.json OR *\/.vault-token OR *\/.config\/Slack\/* OR *\/.config\/discord\/* OR *\/Microsoft\/Teams\/* OR *cookies.sqlite OR *"Login Data"*) -@process.name:(ssh OR sshd OR scp OR sftp OR firefox OR chrome OR chromium OR brave OR slack OR teams OR discord OR keepassxc OR gpg-agent OR git)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo (regex("/\\.ssh/id_", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.npmrc$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.docker/config\\.json$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.vault-token$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/\\.config/(Slack|discord)/", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/Microsoft/Teams/", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("cookies\\.sqlite$", field=TargetFileName) OR regex("/Login Data$", field=TargetFileName))
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/(ssh|sshd|scp|sftp|firefox|chrome|chromium|brave|slack|teams|discord|keepassxc|gpg-agent|git)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctPaths))
| DistinctPaths >= 4
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Microsoft/Teams/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/cookies.sqlite" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Login Data") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("ssh","sshd","ssh-agent","scp","sftp","gpg-agent","git","firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","slack","teams","discord","keepassxc","gnome-keyring-d") by host Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user bin(_time,5m) | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as file_paths values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/known_hosts" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/Slack/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/discord/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Microsoft/Teams/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/cookies.sqlite" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Login Data") AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("ssh","sshd","ssh-agent","scp","sftp","gpg-agent","git","firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","slack","teams","discord","keepassxc","gnome-keyring-d") by host Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.user bin(_time,5m) | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4
Atomic Arch — DNS resolution and HTTP POST to temp.sh from non-browser developer workstation process AICommand & Control High
Detects DNS lookups for temp.sh and HTTP/HTTPS uploads to temp.sh originating from non-browser processes — the Atomic Arch campaign's primary clearnet exfil channel. Browsers/curl-from-shell are noisy on this domain but the 'deps' ELF or an npm/node descendant uploading to it is the campaign signature. Rationale: temp.sh is the article's pre-extracted clearnet exfil domain. Whanos' report and the IFIN summary both flag it as the file-host destination for the archived credential bundles. The non-browser process filter is essential because temp.sh has legitimate human users — the differentiator is that 'deps'/npm/node/curl-from-cron should never POST there from a developer workstation. Cross-checked the .onion + temp.sh dual-channel pattern in the Sonatype writeup. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/ • https://temp.sh/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually uploading a debug log or screenshot to temp.sh via curl/wget for sharing
  • CI/CD job that posts artifacts to temp.sh as part of a lightweight share workflow
  • Security researcher fetching the IOC sample itself from temp.sh for analysis
  • Misconfigured backup script using temp.sh as a poor-man's file drop
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--ci-artifact","DEBUG_SHARE","researcher-sandbox"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full URL path of the POST and the SentBytes to estimate payload size; if multi-MB and the host installed an AUR package in the last 24h, treat as confirmed exfil. Step 2 (contain): Block temp.sh at egress, isolate the host, and pull any temp.sh download URLs the operator may use to retrieve. If the upload URL is recoverable, GET it to capture what was exfiltrated. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep the org for other workstations resolving temp.sh in the last 30 days; correlate with AUR install timestamps from pacman.log; rotate every credential the deps stealer targets (SSH, GitHub, npm, Vault, browser, Slack/Teams/Discord) for any affected user.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has "temp.sh" or RemoteUrl endswith ".temp.sh"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome","firefox","msedge","safari","brave","chromium","opera")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let TempShDNS = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Name has "temp.sh"
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Source="DNS";
let TempShHTTP = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationHostName has "temp.sh" or RequestURL has "temp.sh"
    | where isnotempty(ProcessName) and ProcessName !in~ ("firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","msedge","safari")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=DestinationHostName, RequestURL, RequestMethod, SentBytes, ProcessName, Source="Proxy";
union isfuzzy=true TempShDNS, TempShHTTP
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Atomic Arch — Exfil HTTP POST to temp.sh by Non-Browser Process
id: 3c4d5e6f-7081-9203-b456-7890abcdef01
description: Detects HTTP/HTTPS connections to temp.sh originating from non-browser processes on Linux developer workstations — the clearnet exfil channel of the Atomic Arch supply-chain campaign.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1567.002
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: linux
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationHostname|contains: temp.sh
  filter_browsers:
    Image|endswith:
      - /firefox
      - /chrome
      - /chromium
      - /brave
      - /msedge
      - /safari
  condition: selection and not filter_browsers
level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog) (@network.destination.host:*temp.sh* OR @dns.question.name:*temp.sh*) -@process.name:(firefox OR chrome OR chromium OR brave OR safari OR msedge)
(#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/temp\.sh$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(npm|node|deps|sh|bash|curl|wget)$/i AND NOT ContextImageFileName=/(firefox|chrome|chromium|brave|safari|msedge)$/i)
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/temp\.sh$/i | groupBy([aid], function={ collect([DomainName]) })}, field=aid)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(Web.http_method) as http_method values(Web.user) as user from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*temp.sh*" OR Web.dest="temp.sh" OR Web.site="temp.sh") AND NOT Web.app IN ("firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","safari","msedge") by host Web.app Web.url Web.http_method Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as url values(Web.bytes_out) as bytes_out values(Web.http_method) as http_method values(Web.user) as user from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*temp.sh*" OR Web.dest="temp.sh" OR Web.site="temp.sh") AND NOT Web.app IN ("firefox","chrome","chromium","brave","safari","msedge") by host Web.app Web.url Web.http_method Web.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
Atomic Arch — Tor client spawn or .onion endpoint contact from AUR-installing developer host AICommand & Control High
Detects Tor client/daemon process execution or attempted resolution/contact of the campaign's specific .onion endpoint on hosts that recently installed AUR packages. Tor on a developer workstation is unusual baseline; pairing with the AUR-install context isolates the campaign's hidden-service C2 channel. Rationale: The article and IFIN/Whanos report cite olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion as the Tor hidden-service C2 — that specific 56-char v3 onion string is the campaign's fingerprint. Tor client spawn on a developer workstation that just ran an AUR install is high-fidelity by itself; literal-onion matches are unambiguous. Cross-checked the dual-channel exfil pattern in the Sonatype report. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1090/003/
ATT&CKT1090.003 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running Tor Browser for personal privacy reasons on a BYOD-permitted workstation
  • Researcher analyzing this campaign and resolving the onion address in a sandbox
  • Whistleblower-tooling installations (SecureDrop client) on journalism-focused dev hosts
  • onionshare or similar legitimate file-sharing tooling tested by a user
Suppression filter
| where not(AccountName in~ ("securityresearch","detectiondev") and ProcessCommandLine has "sandbox")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): If the matched string is the literal campaign onion, this is a confirmed C2 contact — escalate immediately. For generic Tor process spawns, check parent chain for pacman/makepkg/npm/node ancestry to disambiguate from human Tor Browser use. Step 2 (contain): Block Tor egress at the firewall (block known Tor entry guards or DPI-block Tor protocol fingerprint), isolate the host, and capture full packet capture from the host's interface for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Search 30 days back for any host org-wide that contacted the campaign onion or any Tor entry guard; cross-reference with the AUR-installing-host list from the pacman.log sweep; rotate every credential class the 'deps' stealer targets for the affected user.
let TorProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("tor","tor.real","torify","torsocks","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client")
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any (".onion","olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid","SocksPort","HiddenServiceDir")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256, Source="Process";
let OnionDNS = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has ".onion" or RemoteUrl has "olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName=InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256=InitiatingProcessSHA256, Source="Network";
union TorProcs, OnionDNS
| order by Timestamp desc
let TorDNS = DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Name has_any (".onion","olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, Source="DNS";
let TorProc = Syslog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ProcessName in~ ("tor","torify","torsocks","obfs4proxy","snowflake-client")
       or SyslogMessage has_any (".onion","olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid","HiddenServiceDir","SocksPort")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, HostName, ProcessName, SyslogMessage, Source="Process";
union isfuzzy=true TorDNS, TorProc
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Atomic Arch — Tor Client or .onion Endpoint Contact
id: 4d5e6f70-8192-a3b4-c567-890abcdef012
description: Detects Tor client process spawn or contact with the Atomic Arch hidden-service C2 onion address.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/over-400-arch-linux-packages-compromised-to-push-rootkit-infostealer/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1090.003
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - /tor
      - /tor.real
      - /torify
      - /torsocks
      - /obfs4proxy
      - /snowflake-client
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - .onion
      - olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid
      - HiddenServiceDir
  condition: selection_proc or selection_cmd
level: high
(source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog) (@process.name:(tor OR torify OR torsocks OR obfs4proxy OR snowflake-client) OR @process.command_line:(*.onion* OR *olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid* OR *HiddenServiceDir*) OR @dns.question.name:*olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid*)
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\/(tor|tor\.real|torify|torsocks|obfs4proxy|snowflake-client)$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 regex("(\.onion|olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid|HiddenServiceDir)", field=CommandLine)) OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, DomainName], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("tor","tor.real","torify","torsocks","obfs4proxy") OR Processes.process="*olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid*" OR Processes.process="*.onion*") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent_process_name values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("tor","tor.real","torify","torsocks","obfs4proxy") OR Processes.process="*olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid*" OR Processes.process="*.onion*") by host Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a

references:

date: 2026/05/02
tags:

logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows

level: critical

        where Web.dest IN ("olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS

    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("olrh4mibs62l6kkuvvjyc5lrercqg5tz543r4lsw3o6mh5qb7g7sneid.onion", "temp.sh")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or MD5 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or SHA1 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40") or MD5 in~ ("6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6144D433F8A0316869877B5F834C801251BBB936E5F1577C5680878C7443C98B", "42B59FDBE1B72895B2951412222EBF40"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] OAuth consent grant to unfamiliar third-party AI / SaaS app — Vercel-style trust chain attack
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud npm worm — shai-hulud-workflow.yml dropped into .github/workflows/ · [LLM] Shai-Hulud bundle.js — known-bad SHA256 written to disk · Suspicious browser extension installation · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Shai-Hulud worm exfil — outbound to webhook.site/bb8ca5f6 from developer or CI process · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TruffleHog binary spawned by npm/node — Shai-Hulud secret harvest · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Shai-Hulud npm worm — shai-hulud-workflow.yml dropped into .github/workflows/ AIInstallation High
Detects the Shai-Hulud self-spreading npm worm's persistence artifact — a GitHub Actions workflow named shai-hulud-workflow.yml written into a repository's .github/workflows/ directory on a developer workstation or CI runner. The workflow re-exfiltrates secrets on every push and is the worm's mechanism for surviving a single npm-package cleanup. Rationale: Filename shai-hulud-workflow.yml in .github/workflows/ is the worm's signature persistence artefact, confirmed by ReversingLabs and Wiz public IOC reports. The article explicitly names Shai-Hulud as the example of npm maintainer compromise. Cross-checked against ReversingLabs and Wiz public IOC bundles. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1053.005 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal security awareness training repo where engineers committed the worm's workflow file as a teaching example
  • Red-team or detection-engineering team intentionally replicating the worm for rule validation
  • Threat-intel researcher pulling the malicious yml down for analysis on a sandbox VM
  • Backup or restore of a previously-cleaned repo where the file lingered in .git history
  • SOC analyst saving the IOC file under a campaign-named folder for documentation
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git.exe","code.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("checkout","pull","clone") and FolderPath has_any ("security-research","redteam","sandbox","ioc-collection"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the file path's parent — was the yml created by git.exe/code.exe (local clone or commit replay, lower urgency) or by node.exe/npm.exe (active worm propagation, contain immediately). Hash the file and compare against 46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke the developer's GitHub PAT and npm token, rotate any cloud credentials cached on the box (AWS, GCP, Azure), and search the developer's GitHub org for any newly-created public repository named 'Shai-Hulud' which holds the exfiltrated data.json. 3) Hunt: across all dev/CI hosts pivot on outbound to webhook.site (see related UC), TruffleHog binary execution under node parentage, and any package the developer publishes — the worm republishes maintained packages to spread.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName =~ "shai-hulud-workflow.yml"
   or FolderPath has @"\.github\workflows\shai-hulud"
   or FolderPath has "/.github/workflows/shai-hulud"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FolderPath, FileName, SHA256,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          GrandParent = InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFileName =~ "shai-hulud-workflow.yml"
   or TargetFilePath has @"\.github\workflows\shai-hulud"
   or TargetFilePath has "/.github/workflows/shai-hulud"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm GitHub Actions Workflow File Drop
id: 7a3b1f88-2c5e-4d29-9b1f-3a8c4e6f12d9
status: experimental
description: Detects creation of the Shai-Hulud worm's shai-hulud-workflow.yml file under .github/workflows/. This workflow is the worm's persistence mechanism — it re-exfiltrates GitHub/npm/cloud tokens to attacker infrastructure on every push.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/early-warning-signs-of-supply-chain-attacks-live-in-the-dark-web/
  - https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm
  - https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.execution

  selection_name:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\shai-hulud-workflow.yml'
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.github\workflows\shai-hulud'
      - '/.github/workflows/shai-hulud'
  condition: selection_name or selection_path
falsepositives:
  - Red-team or security-research lab replicating the Shai-Hulud worm under a campaign-named lab folder
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*shai-hulud-workflow.yml* OR *Shai-Hulud-workflow.yml* OR *SHAI-HULUD-WORKFLOW.YML*)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/shai-hulud-workflow\.yml$/i
| regex("(\\\\|/)\\.github(\\\\|/)workflows(\\\\|/)", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

Shai-Hulud worm exfil — outbound to webhook.site/bb8ca5f6 from developer or CI process AICommand & Control High
Detects outbound HTTPS to the Shai-Hulud worm's documented webhook.site exfiltration endpoint (UUID bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7), or any traffic to webhook.site originating from node/npm/yarn/git on a developer workstation. The worm posts harvested npm/GitHub/AWS/GCP tokens to this endpoint after secrets are scraped. Rationale: webhook.site/bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7 is the canonical Shai-Hulud exfil endpoint per ReversingLabs and Sysdig. The article names Shai-Hulud directly as the worm that 'stole developer secrets' and 'propagated across repositories'. Cross-referenced against multiple public IOC bundles. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/mitigating-risks-shai-hulud-npm-worm
ATT&CKT1567 T1102 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Engineer uses webhook.site for legitimate webhook debugging during third-party integration work
  • CI smoke test posting to a personal webhook.site URL for output capture
  • QA team using webhook.site as a stand-in for an unfinished partner API
  • Security training where the analyst's lab box reproduces the worm's exfil call
  • Browser extension that pings webhook.site as part of its onboarding flow
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("webhook-test","integration-debug","mock-callback") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe","WindowsTerminal.exe","explorer.exe") and not (RemoteUrl has "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm parent — node.exe / runner.exe / npm.exe parentage with no developer-initiated debugging session is the smoking gun. Capture the HTTP body if possible; the worm POSTs a base64 JSON blob of harvested env vars and token files. 2) Contain: isolate, revoke every credential the box has touched in the last 14 days (GitHub PATs, npm tokens, AWS/GCP keys, Azure credentials, Kafka creds, monitoring tokens), and check the developer's GitHub for new public repos named 'Shai-Hulud' containing data.json — delete them immediately and assume the secrets in them are burned. 3) Hunt: pivot org-wide on webhook.site DNS, on any package that this developer publishes (worm propagates by republishing maintained packages), and on bundle.js/SHA256 46faab8ab153... drops across dev fleet.
let ShaiHuludUuid = "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7";
let DevProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where RemoteUrl has "webhook.site"
| where RemoteUrl has ShaiHuludUuid
      or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (DevProcs)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName,
          AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let ShaiHuludUuid = "bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7";
let DevProcs = dynamic(["node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","git.exe","runner.exe","runner.worker.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has "webhook.site"
| where Url has ShaiHuludUuid
      or tolower(tostring(split(SrcUsername,"\\")[-1])) in (DevProcs)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname,
          HttpMethod, Url, HttpRequestBodyBytes, HttpResponseHeaderContentType,
          DstIpAddr, DstHostname
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Shai-Hulud npm Worm Exfiltration to webhook.site Endpoint
id: 5e2c91ad-6d04-4a17-bb43-f31b78c4e09a
status: experimental
description: Detects outbound traffic to the Shai-Hulud worm's documented webhook.site exfiltration UUID, or any webhook.site traffic from a Node/npm/git toolchain process.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/early-warning-signs-of-supply-chain-attacks-live-in-the-dark-web/
  - https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
author: Detection Engineering

tags:

logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_uuid:
    DestinationHostname|contains: 'webhook.site'
    DestinationHostname|contains: 'bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7'

    Image|endswith:

    DestinationHostname|contains: 'webhook.site'

level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.defender) (@DestinationHostname:(*webhook.site/bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7* OR *webhook.site*) OR @RemoteUrl:(*webhook.site/bb8ca5f6-4175-45d2-b042-fc9ebb8170b7* OR *webhook.site*)) AND @Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\npm.exe OR *\yarn.exe OR *\pnpm.exe OR *\git.exe OR *\runner.exe OR *\Runner.Worker.exe OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe)

| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm|git|runner|powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i}, field=ContextProcessId, key=TargetProcessId)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

TruffleHog binary spawned by npm/node — Shai-Hulud secret harvest AIActions on Objectives High
Detects execution of the TruffleHog secret-scanning binary as a child of node.exe / npm.exe / yarn.exe / pnpm.exe / a GitHub Actions runner. The Shai-Hulud worm bundles TruffleHog and runs it post-install to identify and harvest npm / GitHub / AWS / GCP / Azure credentials on developer workstations and CI runners. Rationale: TruffleHog under npm/node parentage is the article-named worm's documented secret-harvest mechanism — confirmed by ReversingLabs, Checkmarx, and Sysdig. Parent-child constraint keeps FPs in DevSecOps pipelines manageable: legitimate scans run under a CI job step with a known runner identity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://checkmarx.com/zero-post/inside-shai-huluds-maw-how-the-npm-worm-exploits-and-propagates/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/shai-hulud-the-novel-self-replicating-worm-infecting-hundreds-of-npm-packages
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sanctioned DevSecOps pipeline running TruffleHog as a pre-merge secret-scan step on a GitHub Actions runner
  • Local developer pre-commit hook running TruffleHog to catch their own leaked secrets
  • Security team performing a hands-on secret audit using TruffleHog under bash/cmd
  • Backup/restore of a CI runner image that includes TruffleHog binary
  • Renovate/Dependabot bot CI runs that include secret-scan tooling
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("trufflehog filesystem --no-update","trufflehog git --no-update") and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("runner.listener.exe","agent.listener.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the exact parent chain — a sanctioned pre-merge pipeline TruffleHog scan has runner.exe → trufflehog with a known repo identity; the worm spawns TruffleHog under node.exe / npm.exe with a postinstall script command line. Hash the binary and check whether it was downloaded fresh into a temp/node_modules path vs the system PATH. 2) Contain: isolate the host, revoke all developer credentials cached on disk (NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS keys, GCP service-account JSON, Azure CLI tokens), and check the developer's GitHub for newly-created repos. 3) Hunt: pivot on webhook.site outbound (see related UC), shai-hulud-workflow.yml drops, bundle.js writes inside node_modules, and any new package version this developer published in the last 72 hours — assume publish chain compromise.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FileName matches regex @"(?i)^trufflehog([0-9])?(\.exe)?$"
        or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog filesystem"
        or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog git"
        or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog --json")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npm-cli.js","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","runner.exe","Runner.Worker.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")

title: TruffleHog Spawned by Node/npm — Shai-Hulud Worm Secret Harvest
id: 9c14a672-3f81-4b56-9aa2-d7e0f24c8a31
status: experimental
description: TruffleHog binary executed as a child of node.exe / npm.exe / yarn.exe / GitHub Actions runner — the Shai-Hulud worm uses TruffleHog to harvest secrets from compromised developer and CI hosts.
references:

falsepositives:

Shai-Hulud bundle.js — known-bad SHA256 written to disk AIInstallation Medium
Hash-based alerting on the Shai-Hulud worm's bundle.js payload. The published SHA256 46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09 is the canonical bundle.js identified by ReversingLabs; additional candidate hashes from this article's IOC bundle are included as likely variants. Targets either the file landing on disk in a node_modules tree or the bundle.js executing under node parentage. Rationale: 46faab8ab153... is the ReversingLabs-confirmed Shai-Hulud bundle.js hash. The article ships an IOC bundle of additional SHA256s consistent with worm-variant reporting; treated here as candidate variants. Behavioural fallback (bundle.js created in node_modules by npm/node parentage) covers hash-rotation cases. Cross-checked against: • https://www.reversinglabs.com/blog/shai-hulud-worm-npm • https://www.wiz.io/blog/shai-hulud-npm-supply-chain-attack • https://cybersecurefox.com/en/shai-hulud-npm-worm-github-actions-supply-chain/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonation of the bundle.js sample on a research host
  • IR forensic image mounted on an analysis machine triggering the hash on read
  • Benign npm package legitimately shipping a bundle.js (hash will not match — behavioural rule only)
  • EDR re-scan of an already-quarantined Shai-Hulud artifact triggering duplicate alerts
  • Detection-engineering lab repo containing the IOC for rule validation
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in ("sandbox-research-01","ir-analysis-01","malware-lab-01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the hash hit is on a real developer/CI host vs a sanctioned research/sandbox machine (allow-list those by hostname). For the behavioural variant — bundle.js in node_modules created by npm/node — pull the parent npm-install command line to identify which package brought the worm in. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill node.exe, quarantine the file, revoke every credential the box has cached (NPM_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS/GCP/Azure keys, Kafka and monitoring tokens), and identify which package shipped it — pull that package version from internal mirrors and notify the broader engineering org not to install. 3) Hunt: pivot on shai-hulud-workflow.yml file drops, webhook.site outbound, TruffleHog spawn under npm parentage, and search the developer's GitHub for new repos named 'Shai-Hulud' containing data.json.

OAuth consent grant to unfamiliar third-party AI / SaaS app — Vercel-style trust chain attack AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the supply-chain pattern called out by the article's Vercel example: a third-party AI tool or SaaS connector receives an OAuth consent grant from a user, gaining cross-tenant access to SaaS scope (mail, files, Graph). Surfaces consent grants to applications never before seen in the tenant, or grants made by non-admin users to apps with high-risk permission scopes. Rationale: Article calls Vercel's April 2026 incident a textbook supply-chain consent abuse — a trusted third-party AI tool with OAuth-connected SaaS access broadening blast radius. Detection anti-joins against tenant's 30-day baseline of seen ApplicationIds and gates on high-risk delegated scopes. Falcon LogScale + Splunk Endpoint datamodels + CloudWatch left empty since the telemetry lives only in AAD audit (no FDR/CIM/AWS analogue).
ATT&CKT1528 T1199 T1078.004
Data sourcesAuthentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT-sanctioned new SaaS onboarding (e.g. a new HR or CRM connector rolling out to a pilot group)
  • Microsoft first-party app newly enabled in the tenant (Copilot variants, Power Platform connectors)
  • Admin testing a new vendor app in a sandbox tenant that shares logs
  • User reconnecting a previously-deleted integration (consent regenerated)
  • Marketplace app installed by a developer for a one-off prototype
Suppression filter
| where TargetApp !in~ ("Microsoft Copilot","Power Automate","Teams Toolkit") and ConsentingUser !in~ ("saas-admin@contoso.com","app-onboarding-svc@contoso.com")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the AppId and look it up against Microsoft's AppId catalog and the tenant's app-governance list. Confirm whether IT/security knew about this app — if yes, allow-list and close. If unknown, examine the publisher domain, the consenting user's recent sign-ins for impossible-travel or risky-state, and whether the consent included offline_access (refresh-token persistence). 2) Contain: revoke the service-principal's consent (Remove-AzureADServicePrincipal or Microsoft Graph DELETE /oauth2PermissionGrants/{id}), invalidate all issued refresh tokens for that user, and block the AppId at the tenant level via conditional-access app filter. 3) Hunt: AADServicePrincipalSignInLogs for the AppId — which mailboxes/files did it actually touch in the last 14 days. OfficeActivity for any MailItemsAccessed by the SP. Search underground monitoring for any post mentioning the tenant or the app publisher.
let Lookback = 30d;
let KnownApps = AADSignInEventsBeta
    | where Timestamp between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(2d))
    | summarize by ApplicationId;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(2d)
| where ActionType has_any ("Consent to application","Add app role assignment grant to user","Add delegated permission grant")
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).Target[0].ID)
| extend ConsentedApp = tostring(ActivityObjects[0].Name),
         ConsentedAppId = tostring(ActivityObjects[0].Id),
         GrantedScopes = tostring(parse_json(tostring(RawEventData)).ModifiedProperties)
| where ConsentedAppId !in (KnownApps)
| where GrantedScopes has_any ("Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Files.Read.All","Files.ReadWrite.All","Sites.Read.All","User.Read.All","Directory.Read.All","offline_access")
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode,
          IsAdminOperation, ConsentedApp, ConsentedAppId, GrantedScopes,
          UserAgent, ActionType
| order by Timestamp desc
let Lookback = 30d;
let KnownApps = SigninLogs
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(Lookback) .. ago(2d))
    | summarize by AppId;
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2d)
| where OperationName in ("Consent to application","Add delegated permission grant","Add app role assignment grant to user")
| extend TargetApp = tostring(TargetResources[0].displayName),
         TargetAppId = tostring(TargetResources[0].id),
         ConsentingUser = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.userPrincipalName),
         IpAddress = tostring(InitiatedBy.user.ipAddress),
         ModifiedProps = tostring(TargetResources[0].modifiedProperties)
| where TargetAppId !in (KnownApps)
| extend HighRiskScope = ModifiedProps has_any ("Mail.Read","Mail.ReadWrite","Files.Read.All","Files.ReadWrite.All","Sites.Read.All","User.Read.All","Directory.Read.All","offline_access","full_access_as_app")
| where HighRiskScope
| project TimeGenerated, ConsentingUser, IpAddress,
          TargetApp, TargetAppId, ModifiedProps, OperationName, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AAD OAuth Consent to Unfamiliar Third-Party App with High-Risk Scopes
id: c4ed7b21-9a30-4d5e-87b1-6e9f4c81207d
status: experimental
description: A user (or admin) consented to a third-party application not previously seen in the tenant, granting high-risk delegated scopes (Mail.*, Files.*, Sites.*, Directory.Read.All, offline_access). Pattern matches Vercel-style supply-chain compromise via OAuth-connected SaaS tools.

        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
