Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33634")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-33634")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2026-33634")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("webhook.site")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["webhook.site"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09", "62ee164b9b306250c1172583f138c9614139264f889fa99614903c12755468d0", "f099c5d9ec417d4445a0328ac0ada9cde79fc37410914103ae9c609cbc0ee068", "cbb9bc5a8496243e02f3cc080efbe3e4a1430ba0671f2e43a202bf45b05479cd", "a3894003ad1d293ba96d77881ccd2071446dc3f65f434669b49b3da92421901a", "b74caeaa75e077c99f7d44f46daaf9796a3be43ecf24f2a1fd381844669da777", "dc67467a39b70d1cd4c1f7f7a459b35058163592f4a9e8fb4dffcbba98ef210c", "4b2399646573bb737c4969563303d8ee2e9ddbd1b271f1ca9e35ea78062538db") or SHA1 in~ ("46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09", "62ee164b9b306250c1172583f138c9614139264f889fa99614903c12755468d0", "f099c5d9ec417d4445a0328ac0ada9cde79fc37410914103ae9c609cbc0ee068", "cbb9bc5a8496243e02f3cc080efbe3e4a1430ba0671f2e43a202bf45b05479cd", "a3894003ad1d293ba96d77881ccd2071446dc3f65f434669b49b3da92421901a", "b74caeaa75e077c99f7d44f46daaf9796a3be43ecf24f2a1fd381844669da777", "dc67467a39b70d1cd4c1f7f7a459b35058163592f4a9e8fb4dffcbba98ef210c", "4b2399646573bb737c4969563303d8ee2e9ddbd1b271f1ca9e35ea78062538db") or MD5 in~ ("46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09", "62ee164b9b306250c1172583f138c9614139264f889fa99614903c12755468d0", "f099c5d9ec417d4445a0328ac0ada9cde79fc37410914103ae9c609cbc0ee068", "cbb9bc5a8496243e02f3cc080efbe3e4a1430ba0671f2e43a202bf45b05479cd", "a3894003ad1d293ba96d77881ccd2071446dc3f65f434669b49b3da92421901a", "b74caeaa75e077c99f7d44f46daaf9796a3be43ecf24f2a1fd381844669da777", "dc67467a39b70d1cd4c1f7f7a459b35058163592f4a9e8fb4dffcbba98ef210c", "4b2399646573bb737c4969563303d8ee2e9ddbd1b271f1ca9e35ea78062538db")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09", "62ee164b9b306250c1172583f138c9614139264f889fa99614903c12755468d0", "f099c5d9ec417d4445a0328ac0ada9cde79fc37410914103ae9c609cbc0ee068", "cbb9bc5a8496243e02f3cc080efbe3e4a1430ba0671f2e43a202bf45b05479cd", "a3894003ad1d293ba96d77881ccd2071446dc3f65f434669b49b3da92421901a", "b74caeaa75e077c99f7d44f46daaf9796a3be43ecf24f2a1fd381844669da777", "dc67467a39b70d1cd4c1f7f7a459b35058163592f4a9e8fb4dffcbba98ef210c", "4b2399646573bb737c4969563303d8ee2e9ddbd1b271f1ca9e35ea78062538db") or SHA1 in~ ("46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09", "62ee164b9b306250c1172583f138c9614139264f889fa99614903c12755468d0", "f099c5d9ec417d4445a0328ac0ada9cde79fc37410914103ae9c609cbc0ee068", "cbb9bc5a8496243e02f3cc080efbe3e4a1430ba0671f2e43a202bf45b05479cd", "a3894003ad1d293ba96d77881ccd2071446dc3f65f434669b49b3da92421901a", "b74caeaa75e077c99f7d44f46daaf9796a3be43ecf24f2a1fd381844669da777", "dc67467a39b70d1cd4c1f7f7a459b35058163592f4a9e8fb4dffcbba98ef210c", "4b2399646573bb737c4969563303d8ee2e9ddbd1b271f1ca9e35ea78062538db") or MD5 in~ ("46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09", "62ee164b9b306250c1172583f138c9614139264f889fa99614903c12755468d0", "f099c5d9ec417d4445a0328ac0ada9cde79fc37410914103ae9c609cbc0ee068", "cbb9bc5a8496243e02f3cc080efbe3e4a1430ba0671f2e43a202bf45b05479cd", "a3894003ad1d293ba96d77881ccd2071446dc3f65f434669b49b3da92421901a", "b74caeaa75e077c99f7d44f46daaf9796a3be43ecf24f2a1fd381844669da777", "dc67467a39b70d1cd4c1f7f7a459b35058163592f4a9e8fb4dffcbba98ef210c", "4b2399646573bb737c4969563303d8ee2e9ddbd1b271f1ca9e35ea78062538db")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["46faab8ab153fae6e80e7cca38eab363075bb524edd79e42269217a083628f09", "62ee164b9b306250c1172583f138c9614139264f889fa99614903c12755468d0", "f099c5d9ec417d4445a0328ac0ada9cde79fc37410914103ae9c609cbc0ee068", "cbb9bc5a8496243e02f3cc080efbe3e4a1430ba0671f2e43a202bf45b05479cd", "a3894003ad1d293ba96d77881ccd2071446dc3f65f434669b49b3da92421901a", "b74caeaa75e077c99f7d44f46daaf9796a3be43ecf24f2a1fd381844669da777", "dc67467a39b70d1cd4c1f7f7a459b35058163592f4a9e8fb4dffcbba98ef210c", "4b2399646573bb737c4969563303d8ee2e9ddbd1b271f1ca9e35ea78062538db"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Agentjacking Attack Tricks AI Coding Agents Into Running Malicious Code

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 11 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have described what they say is a new class of attack that can trick artificial intelligence (AI) coding agents into running arbitrary code on developer machines. Called Agentjacking by Tenet Security, the attack can be triggered by means of a fake error report crafted using Sentry, an open-source error-tracking and performance-monitoring platform. "The attack

Domainsadvisory-tracker.com

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) spawning shell that fetch-and-executes remote payload
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Agentjacking C2/exfiltration to advisory-tracker.com (Tenet Sentry-MCP attack) · [LLM] AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials / env (Agentjacking credential access) · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Agentjacking C2/exfiltration to advisory-tracker.com (Tenet Sentry-MCP attack) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts the Tenet Security 'Agentjacking' exfiltration endpoint that receives developer environment variables, git credentials, repo URLs and tokens stolen by npm typosquat packages that a hijacked AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) was tricked into installing via a forged Sentry issue. Both DNS resolution and TCP egress are pivoted because the npm-installed payload posts to https://advisory-tracker.com/api/v1/telemetry. Rationale: advisory-tracker.com and 52.206.47.180 are the Tenet-published exfiltration endpoint for the Agentjacking PoC, also enumerated in the PSPDFKit IOC repo for the related Sentry npm typosquat campaign. Cross-checked: Tenet's blog post and the PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs GitHub repo both list the same domain + IP + /api/v1/telemetry path, so the IOC has independent corroboration beyond the THN article. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/agentjacking-attacks-hijack-ai/
ATT&CKT1041 T1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised purple-team replay of the Tenet PoC from a research VM
  • Security-research sandbox detonating one of the IOC-listed npm packages
  • Threat-intel enrichment platform (VirusTotal/urlscan) auto-resolving advisory-tracker.com from a SOC analyst workstation
  • DNS-passive-replication sensor logging the domain without an actual host connecting
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\sandbox\", @"\detonation\", @"\threat-research\")) and not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("vt-cli.exe","urlscan.exe","virustotal.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull DeviceProcessEvents for the same DeviceId in the 10 min before the connection, walk the process tree (claude.exe / cursor.exe / code.exe → node.exe → npm/npx → outbound), and confirm the developer was using an AI coding agent against Sentry. 2) Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response; immediately rotate every credential exposed in env on a developer box — git PAT, npm _authToken, AWS/GCP keys, .env secrets, Sentry DSN, any cloud-CLI session token. Quarantine the npm cache and node_modules under the suspect project. 3) Hunt: enumerate every host in the org that resolved advisory-tracker.com or hit 52.206.47.180 in the last 30 days; scan all developer repos for the typosquat package family in package-lock.json / yarn.lock; audit Sentry org membership against affected developers to find the injected issue ID.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has "advisory-tracker.com" or RemoteIP == "52.206.47.180"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
union
  (ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstHostname has "advisory-tracker.com" or DstIpAddr == "52.206.47.180"
    | extend Indicator = coalesce(DstHostname, DstIpAddr)
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImNetworkSession", Host=DvcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator, Url),
  (ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has "advisory-tracker.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="ImDnsActivity", Host=SrcHostname, User=SrcUsername, Indicator=DnsQuery, Url=DnsQuery),
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Name has "advisory-tracker.com"
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsEvents", Host=Computer, User=tostring(""), Indicator=Name, Url=Name)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Agentjacking exfiltration domain advisory-tracker.com resolved
id: 4e3f8d9a-2b1c-4f5e-9d0a-6c7e1f8b2a3d
status: experimental
description: DNS query for advisory-tracker.com, the Tenet 'Agentjacking' exfiltration endpoint receiving developer credentials, environment variables and git tokens posted by npm typosquats installed by a hijacked AI coding agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) after a forged Sentry issue.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/agentjacking-attack-tricks-ai-coding.html
  - https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/
  - https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.exfiltration
  - attack.t1041
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|endswith: 'advisory-tracker.com'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Authorised security-research sandbox detonation of the Tenet PoC
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR linux.auditd OR linux.syslog) AND ((@EventID:3 AND (@DestinationHostname:*advisory-tracker.com OR @DestinationIp:52.206.47.180)) OR (@EventID:22 AND @QueryName:*advisory-tracker.com) OR @network.destination.ip:52.206.47.180)
((#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(^|\.)advisory-tracker\.com$/i) OR (#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="52.206.47.180"))
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId, DomainName, RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="52.206.47.180" OR All_Traffic.dest="advisory-tracker.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.advisory-tracker.com") by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.user, All_Traffic.app, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_ip, All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="advisory-tracker.com" OR DNS.query="*.advisory-tracker.com") by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_ip="52.206.47.180" OR All_Traffic.dest="advisory-tracker.com" OR All_Traffic.dest="*.advisory-tracker.com") by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.user, All_Traffic.app, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_ip, All_Traffic.dest_port | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | append [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS where (DNS.query="advisory-tracker.com" OR DNS.query="*.advisory-tracker.com") by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`] | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime) | sort - lastTime
AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) spawning shell that fetch-and-executes remote payload AIInstallation High
Hunts the Agentjacking execution stage: after a forged Sentry MCP event is rendered as 'Resolution' guidance, the AI coding agent runs the attacker's instruction on the developer's machine. Specifically targets the Claude / Cursor / Codex process tree spawning cmd/PowerShell/bash/node that downloads-and-evaluates remote content (curl|sh, IEX DownloadString, node -e fetch, base64-decoded shell) or directly references the Tenet exfil host. Rationale: Article + Tenet blog both describe AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) reading a forged Sentry 'Resolution' over MCP and executing the attacker's shell command on the developer machine with developer privileges. Anchors on the article-specific parent-process names plus the standard fetch-and-execute payload shapes attacker injections use, and includes the corroborated advisory-tracker.com host so a literal reference fires high-confidence. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.003 T1059.007 T1105 T1204
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer asking the agent to run a legitimate install one-liner from a vendor (e.g. nvm, rustup, ohmyzsh) that uses curl|bash
  • Agent-invoked build step that legitimately uses 'node -e' for codegen
  • PowerShell profile auto-load triggering Invoke-Expression on a vetted helper module
  • Security team running a Tenet PoC replay in a research VM
  • Internal devtools-team approved bootstrap scripts piped through bash
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh","sh.rustup.rs","get.docker.com","raw.githubusercontent.com/ohmyzsh","get-poetry.org")) and not(InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "\\purple-team\\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full parent chain (AI agent → shell → payload), the exact ProcessCommandLine, and any URL it pulled. Pull Sentry MCP request logs for that developer's session to identify the malicious issue ID; correlate to inbound POSTs to /api/0/store/ or /api/0/envelope/ on Sentry. 2) Contain: kill the descendant tree via Live Response; suspend the developer's AI-agent session; revoke every credential touchable from that shell context (git PAT, npm _authToken, AWS/GCP CLI tokens, SSH keys); quarantine downloaded artefacts and any new node_modules. 3) Hunt: pivot on the fetched URL, npm package name, and command hash across the dev fleet; query Sentry to see if the same injected issue body appears in other projects; audit which developers asked the agent to 'fix Sentry issues' in the last 14 days and verify their machines.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe"))
    or (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
        and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd"))
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-Expression","IEX(","IEX (","DownloadString","Net.WebClient","| sh","| bash","|sh ","|bash ","node -e","base64 -d","bash -c","powershell -enc","powershell -e ","powershell -EncodedCommand","curl -s ","wget -qO","advisory-tracker.com")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandparentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
     or (ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd") and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("claude","cursor","codex"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-Expression","IEX(","IEX (","DownloadString","Net.WebClient","| sh","| bash","|sh ","|bash ","node -e","base64 -d","bash -c","powershell -enc","powershell -EncodedCommand","curl -s","wget -qO","advisory-tracker.com")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AI coding agent spawning shell that fetch-and-executes remote payload (Agentjacking)

status: experimental
description: AI coding agent (Claude Code / Cursor / Codex) parent process spawning cmd / PowerShell / bash / node that downloads-and-evaluates remote content or references the Tenet Agentjacking exfil host. The forged Sentry MCP 'Resolution' tricks the agent into executing this on the developer machine.

  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/agentjacking-attack-tricks-ai-coding.html
  - https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/

detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\claude.exe'
      - '\Claude.exe'
      - '\cursor.exe'
      - '\Cursor.exe'
      - '\code.exe'
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\codex.exe'
      - '\claude-code.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:

      - '\powershell.exe'

      - '\sh.exe'

      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'Net.WebClient'
      - '| sh'
      - '| bash'
      - 'node -e'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:1 AND @ParentImage:(*\\claude.exe OR *\\Claude.exe OR *\\cursor.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\codex.exe OR *\\claude-code.exe) AND @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npx.cmd OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe) AND @CommandLine:(*Invoke-Expression* OR *IEX* OR *DownloadString* OR *Net.WebClient* OR *"| sh"* OR *"| bash"* OR *"node -e"* OR *"base64 -d"* OR *"bash -c"* OR *"powershell -enc"* OR *"powershell -EncodedCommand"* OR *advisory-tracker.com*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(claude|cursor|code|codex|claude-code)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(cmd|powershell|pwsh|bash|sh|node|npm|npx|curl|wget)\.(exe|cmd)$/i
| regex("(?i)(Invoke-Expression|IEX\\s*\\(|DownloadString|Net\\.WebClient|\\|\\s*(sh|bash)\\b|node\\s+-e|base64\\s+-d|bash\\s+-c|powershell\\s+-(e|enc|EncodedCommand)|advisory-tracker\\.com)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials / env (Agentjacking credential access) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the Agentjacking credential_access stage where the hijacked AI agent's child process dumps environment variables and reads developer secret files — the specific data Tenet showed exfiltrated (env vars, git credentials, private repo URLs, AWS/cloud keys, npm _authToken, .env contents). Independent of the exfil IOC so it survives C2 rotation. Rationale: Tenet's writeup explicitly names the exfiltrated data classes — environment variables, Git credentials, private repository URLs, developer identities — which directly map to the file/env paths in this query. By anchoring on AI-coding-agent parents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) reading these specific resources, the detection survives even if the attacker rotates the advisory-tracker.com IOC. SENTRY_DSN is included because that's the bootstrap secret a typosquat would harvest first. Cross-checked against: • https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/agentjacking-attacks-hijack-ai/ • https://github.com/PSPDFKit/sentry-npm-typosquat-2026-06-iocs
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1555 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer legitimately asking Claude/Cursor to debug a git auth failure (printenv / git config --get)
  • AI agent reading .npmrc _authToken to scope a sanctioned npm install
  • aws-cli / gcloud-cli config inspection invoked at developer request
  • ohmyzsh / shell-init scripts that printenv on session start under an agent terminal
  • CI emulator running inside Cursor terminal that dumps env for build context
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("git config --global credential.helper","git config --get user.email","aws configure list","gcloud auth list")) and not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--debug-auth")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm parent chain (Claude/Cursor/Codex/node → shell → cred read) and verify the command-line wasn't a developer-issued debug step. Pull the Sentry MCP tool-call history for the developer's session and locate the issue body whose 'Resolution' text seeded the command. 2) Contain: rotate every credential whose file or env-var was read — git PAT, AWS/GCP CLI keys, SSH private keys, .env secrets, npm _authToken, the Sentry DSN itself. Force the developer to re-auth into all coding sessions and invalidate the host's OS keyring. 3) Hunt: across the dev fleet, find every AI-agent descendant that read the same credential paths in the last 30 days; correlate against outbound traffic from the same process tree to advisory-tracker.com and to any unfamiliar /api/v1/telemetry endpoint; audit the org's Sentry projects for forged issues containing markdown resolution sections.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
    or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentProcess = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          GrandparentProcess = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ChildProcess = FileName,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("claude.exe","cursor.exe","code.exe","codex.exe","claude-code.exe","node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (
    "Get-ChildItem Env:","Get-ChildItem env:","ls env:","printenv","$env:",
    "type .env","cat .env","Get-Content .env",
    ".git-credentials","git config --global credential","git remote -v",
    @".aws\credentials",".aws/credentials",
    @".ssh\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",@".ssh\id_ed25519",".ssh/id_ed25519",
    ".npmrc","_authToken","SENTRY_DSN"
  )
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AI coding agent descendant reading developer credentials (Agentjacking)
id: c8d2e3f4-a5b6-4c7d-8e9f-0a1b2c3d4e5f
status: experimental
description: Detects descendants of AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) dumping environment variables or reading developer credential files (.git-credentials, .aws/credentials, .ssh keys, .env, .npmrc _authToken) — the credential_access stage of Tenet's 'Agentjacking' attack where a forged Sentry MCP event hijacks the agent.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/agentjacking-attack-tricks-ai-coding.html
  - https://tenetsecurity.ai/blog/agentjacking-coding-agents-with-fake-sentry-errors/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.credential_access
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1552.004
  - attack.t1555
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\claude.exe'
      - '\Claude.exe'
      - '\cursor.exe'
      - '\Cursor.exe'
      - '\code.exe'
      - '\Code.exe'
      - '\codex.exe'
      - '\claude-code.exe'
      - '\node.exe'
      - '\npm.cmd'
      - '\npx.cmd'
  selection_cred:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Get-ChildItem Env:'
      - 'ls env:'
      - 'printenv'
      - '$env:'
      - '.git-credentials'
      - 'git config --global credential'
      - 'git remote -v'
      - '.aws\credentials'
      - '.aws/credentials'
      - '.ssh\id_rsa'
      - '.ssh/id_rsa'
      - '.ssh\id_ed25519'
      - '.ssh/id_ed25519'
      - '.npmrc'
      - '_authToken'
      - 'cat .env'
      - 'type .env'
      - 'Get-Content .env'
      - 'SENTRY_DSN'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_cred
falsepositives:
  - Developer asking the AI agent to debug authentication / env config
  - Agent extension legitimately reading .npmrc tokens during a sanctioned install
  - aws-cli / gcloud-cli helper invoked by the agent on the developer's instruction
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon AND @EventID:1 AND @ParentImage:(*\\claude.exe OR *\\Claude.exe OR *\\cursor.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe OR *\\code.exe OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\codex.exe OR *\\claude-code.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npx.cmd) AND @CommandLine:(*"Get-ChildItem Env:"* OR *"ls env:"* OR *printenv* OR *".git-credentials"* OR *".aws\\credentials"* OR *".aws/credentials"* OR *".ssh\\id_rsa"* OR *".ssh/id_rsa"* OR *".ssh\\id_ed25519"* OR *".ssh/id_ed25519"* OR *"git remote -v"* OR *".npmrc"* OR *_authToken* OR *"cat .env"* OR *"type .env"* OR *SENTRY_DSN*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(claude|cursor|code|codex|claude-code|node|npm|npx)\.(exe|cmd)$/i
| regex("(?i)(Get-ChildItem\\s+Env:|ls\\s+env:|printenv|\\$env:[A-Za-z_]|\\.git-credentials\\b|git\\s+config\\s+--global\\s+credential|git\\s+remote\\s+-v|\\.aws[\\\\/]credentials|\\.ssh[\\\\/]id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|\\.npmrc\\b|_authToken|cat\\s+\\.env\\b|type\\s+\\.env\\b|Get-Content\\s+\\.env|SENTRY_DSN)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600

Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("advisory-tracker.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["advisory-tracker.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

    from datamodel=Web

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)

| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Rethinking MDR as Attackers and Defenders Embrace AI

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 9 use cases 6 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

For most of the past decade, managed detection and response was the answer to a real problem. Security teams couldn't staff around the clock, couldn't hire enough analysts, and needed someone else to handle the alert queue. MDR stepped in. It worked well enough. Until now. The threat landscape has changed faster than the MDR model can adapt. Attackers are using AI to move faster, generate more

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

author: Clankerusecase

            - '\psexesvc.exe'

            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

falsepositives:

       OR (Processes.process_name="wmic.exe" AND Processes.process="*/node:*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

LangGraph Flaw Chain Exposes Self-Hosted AI Agents to Remote Code Execution

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 11 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of three now-patched security flaws impacting LangGraph, including a critical vulnerability chain that could result in remote code execution. LangGraph is an open-source framework created by LangChain to build complex, stateful, and multi-agent artificial intelligence (AI) agentic applications. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] LangGraph get_state_history SQLi via metadata filter (CVE-2025-67644) · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children

LangGraph get_state_history SQLi via metadata filter (CVE-2025-67644) AIExploitation High
Hunts inbound HTTP requests to a self-hosted LangGraph server's get_state_history endpoint where the metadata filter parameter carries SQL injection syntax. Targets the first step of the published RCE chain — manipulating the SQLite checkpoint query to return an attacker-controlled BLOB. Rationale: Article explicitly names the get_state_history() endpoint and identifies CVE-2025-67644 as a SQLi in metadata filter keys against the SQLite checkpointer. The URL-substring set covers union-based and tautology payloads that any working exploit would emit. defender_kql is empty because Defender Advanced Hunting has no inbound HTTP request body table; sentinel ImWebSession is the right pivot.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security scanner runs (Burp, sqlmap, internal DAST) hitting LangGraph endpoints
  • Developers debugging the get_state_history endpoint with literal SQL keywords in filter strings
  • Pen-testing engagements with documented scope
  • Test fixtures that embed UNION/SELECT in payloads stored as filter values
  • Web spider crawling the LangGraph admin UI
Suppression filter
and SrcIpAddr !in ("<scanner_ip_1>", "<scanner_ip_2>") and HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("sqlmap", "Burp", "ZAP")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the source IP is not an approved scanner/pen-test source; pull the full request URL, body, response status and any subsequent process spawned by the LangGraph runtime within 30s on the target host. 2) Contain: if status was 200 and the runtime PID then forked a shell/curl/wget (see UC2), isolate the host via MDE LiveResponse and snapshot the SQLite checkpoint DB before it is overwritten. 3) Hunt: pivot the source IP across ImWebSession for any other LangGraph endpoints touched in the last 30 days; review checkpoints table for rows whose metadata column contains opcode markers (\x80, \x95) suggesting an injected msgpack BLOB.
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has "get_state_history"
| where Url has "filter"
| where Url has_any ("UNION", "SELECT", "%27", "--", "DROP", "sqlite_master", "%20OR%20", "%20AND%20")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Shell/LOLBin spawned by LangGraph Python or Node runtime AIInstallation High
Detects classic post-RCE behaviour where a LangGraph runtime process (python/uvicorn/node executing a langgraph entrypoint) spawns a shell or download utility. Anchors to parent command lines containing langgraph/langchain/checkpoint so it does not fire on generic python workloads. Rationale: Article describes RCE achieved after chained SQLi+deserialization where the malicious msgpack payload runs in the LangGraph application runtime. Anchoring on python/uvicorn/node parents with langgraph/langchain/checkpoint/get_state_history in the parent cmdline keeps this from firing on generic dev environments. The LOLBin child set is the standard post-exec pivot.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1059.004 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Data scientists running interactive notebooks that shell out via subprocess from a langchain pipeline
  • CI jobs in langgraph repos invoking shell during tests or build
  • Custom langgraph tools that legitimately wrap curl/bash (web-fetch, k8s exec tooling)
  • Operators running troubleshooting commands inside a running uvicorn container via docker exec — parent reparented to python
  • langgraph-cli launching helper utilities like git or pip during package install
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langgraph-cli", "langgraph dev", "langgraph build") and FileName in~ ("git.exe", "pip.exe", "pip3"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full ParentCommandLine + ChildCmd, confirm the LangGraph server PID's listening port and whether get_state_history was hit in the last 5 minutes (cross-reference UC1). Check whether the child command line includes base64, /dev/tcp/, or python -c — strong RCE signal. 2) Contain: isolate the host via MDE LiveResponse, dump the running python process memory (procdump) to preserve the deserialized payload, kill the runtime PID. 3) Hunt: search for any FileWritten by the same PID in the prior 60 minutes (UC5), enumerate other hosts running the same langgraph-checkpoint-sqlite version (UC3) and any outbound network the runtime opened (UC4).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","python3.exe","pythonw.exe","python","python3","uvicorn","uvicorn.exe","node.exe","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langgraph","langchain","checkpoint","get_state_history")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","bash.exe","sh","bash","curl.exe","wget.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat.exe","certutil.exe","chmod","chmod.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","uvicorn","node")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("langgraph","langchain","checkpoint","get_state_history")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langgraph","langchain","checkpoint","get_state_history")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh","cmd.exe","bash","sh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","certutil.exe","chmod")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects shell or download LOLBins spawned by a LangGraph/LangChain runtime process — possible RCE via the CVE-2025-67644 + CVE-2026-28277 chain.
references:

author: SOC
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

logsource:

detection:

      - '\python3.exe'
      - '\pythonw.exe'

      - '\wget.exe'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\python.exe OR *\\Python.exe OR *\\python3.exe OR *\\uvicorn.exe OR *\\node.exe) (@ParentCommandLine:*langgraph* OR @ParentCommandLine:*langchain* OR @ParentCommandLine:*checkpoint* OR @ParentCommandLine:*get_state_history*) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\bash.exe OR *\\sh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\certutil.exe)

| ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|bash|sh|curl|wget|nc|ncat|certutil)(\.exe)?$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ParentCommandLine, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
