PowerShell process invoking LDAP:// with hardcoded plaintext credential AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts PowerShell processes whose command line contains an LDAP:// URI together with credential-binding constructs (DirectoryEntry, ConvertTo-SecureString, NetworkCredential, -Password). Directly mirrors the article's report that the stolen Tchap data included a PowerShell script with hardcoded LDAP credentials — same pattern across the estate is both a leaked-secret indicator and a credential-access TTP. Rationale: Article explicitly states the dumped Tchap data included 'hardcoded LDAP credentials leaked via a PowerShell script' — this query finds the same anti-pattern across the org so it can be remediated before a similar leak. LDAP:// + DirectoryEntry/ConvertTo-SecureString is the canonical AD-bind PowerShell pattern and is extremely low-FP outside of legacy admin scripts. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy AD admin scripts that legitimately bind via DirectoryEntry with a credential param (should be migrated to gMSA)
  • Vendor installers/configurators (e.g. Quest, ManageEngine) that test LDAP bind during install
  • DSC/Ansible AD-join modules invoking ConvertTo-SecureString against LDAP://
  • PowerShell ISE / VSCode user testing an LDAP query interactively with credentials in cleartext
  • SCCM/Intune compliance scripts probing AD with bound credentials
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Program Files\Microsoft Configuration Manager\" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Quest\"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the full ProcessCommandLine and the script path (FolderPath). Pull the script file from the host and grep for the literal credential string — confirm whether it's a real bind credential or a placeholder. Step 2 (contain): If the credential is real, immediately reset that AD account's password and audit its group memberships. If the script is in a shared location (SYSVOL, file share, Git repo), purge all copies and check git history. Step 3 (hunt): Search EmailEvents/ProxyLogs for any outbound upload of the script file SHA256 (e.g. to GitHub, paste sites, Tchap). Pivot on the AD account name through DeviceLogonEvents to spot any subsequent suspicious binds from non-admin hosts.
let LdapMarker = "LDAP://";
let CredMarkers = dynamic(["DirectoryEntry","DirectorySearcher","ConvertTo-SecureString","NetworkCredential","-Password","PrincipalContext","AccountManagement"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has LdapMarker or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has LdapMarker
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (CredMarkers) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (CredMarkers)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LdapMarker = "LDAP://";
let CredMarkers = dynamic(["DirectoryEntry","DirectorySearcher","ConvertTo-SecureString","NetworkCredential","-Password","PrincipalContext","AccountManagement"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe" or ParentProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine has LdapMarker
| where CommandLine has_any (CredMarkers)
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: PowerShell Script Hardcoding LDAP Bind Credentials
id: a8f3c1b2-7d4e-4f9c-9b8a-2c3d4e5f6a7b
description: PowerShell process command line referencing an LDAP:// URI together with credential-binding cmdlets/strings, mirroring the hardcoded LDAP credentials reported leaked in the 2026 Tchap breach.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/french-govt-says-tchap-breach-affected-over-73-000-accounts/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_ps:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_ldap:
    CommandLine|contains: 'LDAP://'
  selection_cred:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'DirectoryEntry'
      - 'DirectorySearcher'
      - 'ConvertTo-SecureString'
      - 'NetworkCredential'
      - '-Password'
      - 'PrincipalContext'
  condition: selection_ps and selection_ldap and selection_cred
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe) @CommandLine:(*LDAP\:\/\/*) @CommandLine:(*DirectoryEntry* OR *DirectorySearcher* OR *ConvertTo-SecureString* OR *NetworkCredential* OR *Password* OR *PrincipalContext*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/LDAP:\/\//i
| CommandLine=/(DirectoryEntry|DirectorySearcher|ConvertTo-SecureString|NetworkCredential|-Password|PrincipalContext)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=[min(_time), max(_time), count()])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") Processes.process="*LDAP://*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search process_cmd="*DirectoryEntry*" OR process_cmd="*DirectorySearcher*" OR process_cmd="*ConvertTo-SecureString*" OR process_cmd="*NetworkCredential*" OR process_cmd="*-Password*" OR process_cmd="*PrincipalContext*" | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") Processes.process="*LDAP://*" by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | search process_cmd="*DirectoryEntry*" OR process_cmd="*DirectorySearcher*" OR process_cmd="*ConvertTo-SecureString*" OR process_cmd="*NetworkCredential*" OR process_cmd="*-Password*" OR process_cmd="*PrincipalContext*" | sort - lastTime
Multi-GB outbound transfer from single user to Tchap/Matrix endpoint (exfil volume) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Flags accounts pulling >1GB cumulative response bytes from tchap.gouv.fr or matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr in a 4-hour window. Calibrated to the 13.5GB of documents/media the actor exfiltrated — a normal civil servant downloads <100MB/day from Tchap. Sentinel query relies on proxy/CommonSecurityLog because Defender DeviceNetworkEvents doesn't carry per-flow bytes consistently. Rationale: Article quantifies the exfil as '13.5GB of documents and media files' — the 1GB/4h threshold is well below the total but well above any normal civil-servant Tchap usage (Tchap is chat+small attachments, not a file server). Anchored on the two confirmed Tchap domains in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://www.numerique.gouv.fr/actualites/securite-de-tchap-derniere-mise-a-jour-au-9-juin-2026/
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1020 T1030
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A user joining a video meeting room with a long media history downloading cached attachments on /sync
  • Tchap mobile-to-desktop migration syncing message history for the first time
  • Power user who is member of large file-heavy public rooms doing legitimate catch-up after vacation
  • Backup/eDiscovery tooling pulling rooms on behalf of compliance team
  • A misconfigured Matrix federation peer pulling history under a user token
Suppression filter
| where SourceUserName !in~ (dynamic(["compliance-svc","ediscovery-svc","backup-svc"]))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Compare the user's prior 30-day baseline of Tchap bytes — confirm the 4h window is a real outlier, not just a heavy-attachment room. Check whether the source IP matches their normal corporate/VPN exit. Step 2 (contain): If outlier confirmed and source IP is anomalous, freeze the Tchap session via DINUM, force MFA reset, and snapshot the device for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the source IP through proxy logs to find any subsequent upload to file-sharing services (mega.nz, anonfiles, IPFS, paste sites) within 24h — that's where the 13.5GB would have landed.
let TchapDomains = dynamic(["tchap.gouv.fr", "matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (TchapDomains)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp),
            LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            DurationMin = datetime_diff('minute', max(Timestamp), min(Timestamp))
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 4h)
| where ConnCount > 2000 and DurationMin between (5 .. 240)
| extend ConnsPerMin = round(todouble(ConnCount) / max_of(DurationMin, 1), 1)
| order by ConnCount desc
let TchapDomains = dynamic(["tchap.gouv.fr", "matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr"]);
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationDnsDomain has_any (TchapDomains) or RequestURL has_any (TchapDomains)
| where isnotempty(SourceUserName) and SourceUserName !endswith "$"
| summarize TotalReceivedBytes = sum(ReceivedBytes),
            TotalSentBytes = sum(SentBytes),
            ConnCount = count(),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SourceUserName, SourceIP, bin(TimeGenerated, 4h)
| where TotalReceivedBytes > 1073741824
| extend ReceivedGB = round(todouble(TotalReceivedBytes) / 1073741824.0, 2)
| order by TotalReceivedBytes desc
source:(zscaler OR proxy OR paloalto OR fortinet) @network.destination.name:(tchap.gouv.fr OR matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr) @network.bytes_read:>=1073741824
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|curl|wget|python|python3|node)\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(tchap\.gouv\.fr|matrix\.agent\.education\.tchap\.gouv\.fr)/i | groupBy([aid, FirstIP4Record], function=count()) | rename(FirstIP4Record, as=RemoteAddressIP4)}, field=[aid, RemoteAddressIP4])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
| _count > 2000
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true sum(All_Traffic.bytes_in) as bytes_in sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("tchap.gouv.fr","matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user _time span=4h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where bytes_in > 1073741824 | eval gb_in=round(bytes_in/1073741824,2) | sort - bytes_in
| tstats summariesonly=false sum(All_Traffic.bytes_in) as bytes_in sum(All_Traffic.bytes_out) as bytes_out count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest IN ("tchap.gouv.fr","matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.user _time span=4h | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | where bytes_in > 1073741824 | eval gb_in=round(bytes_in/1073741824,2) | sort - bytes_in
Bulk Matrix profile/room-member enumeration against Tchap endpoint AIReconnaissance Medium
Detects scripted enumeration of the Matrix /profile, /joined_members, /members and /state endpoints on the Tchap Matrix server — the exact API path the attacker walked to harvest the 73,467 affected users' names, emails, avatars and organizations. Requires proxy-level URL visibility (Sentinel ImWebSession / CommonSecurityLog) because Defender DeviceNetworkEvents only carries the hostname. Rationale: Article enumerates the exact data classes stolen — 'last name, first name, email address, belonging entity and avatar' — these correspond to Matrix /profile/{userId} (display name+avatar) and /joined_members (membership+display name) on a per-room basis. Repeated calls to these endpoints from one account is the only way to assemble a 73k-account roster of who-works-where. Cross-checked against: • https://spec.matrix.org/v1.6/client-server-api/#get_matrixclientv3roomsroomidjoined_members • https://www.numerique.gouv.fr/actualites/securite-de-tchap-derniere-mise-a-jour-au-9-juin-2026/
ATT&CKT1087 T1087.004 T1213
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Tchap admin/moderator tooling enumerating room membership for governance reports
  • Matrix federation health-check probes calling /joined_members at fixed intervals
  • User opening many public rooms in quick succession (Element fetches member lists per room)
  • Compliance/eDiscovery service account exporting member rosters
  • Mobile client doing initial /sync with member-list expansion enabled
Suppression filter
| where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Element/","Tchap/","Riot/","matrix-android-sdk","matrix-ios-sdk")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Inspect the user-agent on the matching requests — Element/Tchap official clients carry recognisable UA strings; a generic Go-http-client / python-requests / curl UA is a strong actor signal. Confirm the user account has any business reason to enumerate cross-ministry rooms. Step 2 (contain): If the UA is scripted or the account is enumerating outside its own ministry, freeze the Tchap session via DINUM and pull the host for forensics. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot on the rooms enumerated — any room hit by this account that the user isn't a documented member of widens the breach scope. Search EmailEvents and proxy uploads for any subsequent dump of the enumerated user list to external sites.
let TchapDomains = dynamic(["tchap.gouv.fr", "matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr"]);
let ScriptedClients = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","node.exe","httpie.exe","go.exe"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (TchapDomains)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (ScriptedClients)
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/_matrix/client/","/joined_members","/profile/","/members")
| summarize ConnCount = count(), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where ConnCount > 50
| order by ConnCount desc
let TchapDomains = dynamic(["tchap.gouv.fr", "matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr"]);
let EnumPaths = dynamic(["/profile/","/joined_members","/members","/state","/messages","/_matrix/client/"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Url has_any (TchapDomains) or DstHostname has_any (TchapDomains)
| where Url has_any (EnumPaths)
| where isnotempty(SrcUsername)
| summarize ProfileQueries = countif(Url has "/profile/"),
            MemberQueries = countif(Url has "/joined_members" or Url has "/members"),
            RoomStateQueries = countif(Url has "/state" or Url has "/messages"),
            TotalQueries = count(),
            DistinctRooms = dcountif(Url, Url has "/rooms/"),
            UAs = make_set(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, 5),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated),
            LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by SrcUsername, SrcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where (ProfileQueries + MemberQueries) > 250 or TotalQueries > 1000
| order by TotalQueries desc
source:(zscaler OR proxy OR paloalto OR fortinet) @network.destination.name:(tchap.gouv.fr OR matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr) @http.url:(*\/_matrix\/client\/* OR *\/joined_members* OR *\/profile\/* OR *\/members*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|curl|wget|python|python3|node)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(tchap\.gouv\.fr|matrix\.agent\.education\.tchap\.gouv\.fr)/i
| CommandLine=/(\/_matrix\/client\/|\/joined_members|\/profile\/|\/members|\/state)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest IN ("tchap.gouv.fr","matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr") (Web.url="*/profile/*" OR Web.url="*/joined_members*" OR Web.url="*/members*" OR Web.url="*/state*" OR Web.url="*/messages*") by Web.src Web.user _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count > 500 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.dest IN ("tchap.gouv.fr","matrix.agent.education.tchap.gouv.fr") (Web.url="*/profile/*" OR Web.url="*/joined_members*" OR Web.url="*/members*" OR Web.url="*/state*" OR Web.url="*/messages*") by Web.src Web.user _time span=1h | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where count > 500 | sort - count
PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"

          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027

logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"

Europol Disrupts AudiA6 Crypto Laundering Service Used by Ransomware Gangs

The Hacker News
2026-06-12 13 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Authorities in Europe have disrupted AudiA6, a cryptocurrency laundering service used by ransomware gangs and cybercriminal networks. Europol, in a statement issued Thursday, said the dismantling of AudiA6 cut off a "key financial pipeline used to wash hundreds of millions in illicit profits." The service is estimated to have been used to launder more than €336 million (~$389 million) since the

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Inbound or outbound email involving AudiA6 mule-recruitment domains · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS/network contact with AudiA6 money-mule registration domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
DNS/network contact with AudiA6 money-mule registration domains AICommand & Control High
Detects endpoints resolving or connecting to the 19 email-infrastructure domains Europol linked to the AudiA6 crypto-laundering service. These domains were used to register fraudulent KYC accounts at cryptocurrency exchanges; a corporate device touching them indicates either an insider acting as a money mule, attacker reuse of corporate infrastructure for laundering, or recruitment communications reaching staff. Rationale: All 19 domains are taken verbatim from the Europol statement in the article body — they are confirmed by a primary law-enforcement source naming them as AudiA6-controlled infrastructure for mule account registration. No second-source web search was performed; the IOC list IS the primary-source bulletin. The domains are unusual second-level / vanity TLDs (.pictures, .top, .click, .agency, .express, .black, .email) so corporate baseline noise is near-zero, justifying alerting tier.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1583.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst manually browsing the Europol seizure page or VirusTotal pivot from a security workstation
  • Compliance / fraud team performing mule-account research against the published domain list
  • Researcher visiting the post-takedown Europol seizure banner now hosted on the seized domains
  • Honeypot / sinkhole resolution sweeps from a security tooling host enumerating IOC lists
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessAccountName !has_any ("soc","threatintel","fraud","compliance")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): identify the resolving process and user — if InitiatingProcessFileName is a browser and the user belongs to security / fraud / compliance, check if they were actively reviewing the Europol bulletin (corroborate with browser history or ticket activity). Pull the device's user-context: insider risk score, finance/payments role, prior crypto-exchange traffic. Step 2 (contain): if the user is not a security researcher, isolate the device via Defender / Falcon Network Containment, suspend the AAD account, and block all 19 domains at the proxy/DNS layer pending review. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the device's last 30 days for outbound traffic to crypto-exchange APIs (binance, kraken, coinbase, kucoin), email to/from these same domains, and any KYC document uploads from the device; also sweep the org for any other host that resolved the same domain.

DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend HostLower = tolower(RemoteUrl)
| where HostLower has_any (AudiA6Domains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc

  (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | extend QueryLower = tolower(Name) | where QueryLower has_any (AudiA6Domains) | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname = Computer, SrcIpAddr = ClientIP, Query = Name, ResponseCode = ResultCode, Source = "DnsEvents")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Inbound or outbound email involving AudiA6 mule-recruitment domains AIDelivery High
Detects email events where the sender or recipient domain matches one of the 19 AudiA6-controlled email domains identified by Europol. Article specifies these domains were used to register money-mule cryptocurrency exchange accounts using stolen identities and that Russian-speaking intermediaries were recruited via them — corporate email touching these domains indicates either mule-recruitment outreach or a staff member operating accounts on behalf of the laundering ring. Rationale: Article explicitly states AudiA6 'relied on both commercial email providers and email addresses linked to domains under their control to register money mule accounts' and recruited 'Russian-speaking intermediaries' via these channels — so inbound mail FROM these domains is recruitment outreach and outbound mail TO them is staff operating as mules. Sentinel KQL left empty because the provided Sentinel schema reference does not list a clean mailflow table (OfficeActivity covers admin operations, not full inbound metadata); operators on M365D-connected Sentinel tenants can re-use the Defender query verbatim against the imported EmailEvents table. Datadog/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty as none of those platforms ship M365 mailflow telemetry in the schemas referenced. Sigma skipped because Sigma's email logsource has no portable cross-vendor sender-domain selector matching this shape.
ATT&CKT1585.002 T1566
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Anti-fraud or threat-intel team mailing the AudiA6 domains for IOC validation / takedown coordination
  • A legitimate small SaaS that shared infrastructure on a generic vanity TLD (low risk given Europol seizure but possible for residual MX records on .email/.top domains)
  • Researcher subscribing a personal corporate mailbox to a blog newsletter that happens to send from one of the seized vanity domains pre-takedown
  • Quarantined / blocked spam that EmailEvents still records as a delivery attempt (DeliveryAction == Blocked) — analyst should treat these as a hit but lower severity
Suppression filter
| where not (RecipientEmailAddress has_any ("abuse@","soc@","threatintel@","fraud@") and EmailDirection == "Inbound")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): pull the full message body via Threat Explorer / Content Search, check EmailDirection (Inbound = likely recruitment, Outbound = potential mule activity by the user). Examine sender display name, language (article notes Russian-speaking intermediaries), and any crypto-wallet addresses or exchange-platform links in the body. Step 2 (contain): if Outbound from an internal user, suspend the AAD account and seize the mailbox for forensics; if Inbound and delivered, soft-delete from all recipient mailboxes via Threat Explorer and add the sender domain to the tenant block-list. Step 3 (hunt): pivot on the recipient/sender user — pull their 90-day SigninLogs for unusual geo, AAD app consents to crypto-wallet/exchange OAuth apps, and any DLP hits on outbound files containing identity documents (passport scans, utility bills) which are the KYC artifacts AudiA6 needed for mule registration.

ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

SecurityEvent

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling
| order by files desc

ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where EventType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(TargetFileName)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.user, _time span=1m
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: LSASS Process Access Outside Microsoft-Signed Tooling
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d04
status: experimental
description: |
    Anything opening lsass.exe with read-memory access that isn't a
    Microsoft signed component (Defender, csrss, etc.) is suspect.
    Mimikatz / Pypykatz / nanodump signature.

Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:

      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
